Reading this manual

Polyphase Float is a C library for computations whose precision, rounding, and resource use need to be explicit. It stores binary floating-point values at a precision chosen by the application and provides arithmetic, elementary and selected special functions, constants, conversion, text formatting, and binary interchange. Its core uses GMP for exact integer machinery and does not call MPFR. An optional adapter moves values between the two libraries.

The first part of this book develops a working application from initialization through checked results and cleanup. The middle chapters explain numerical workflows, storage, threads, and integration. The final part contains the numerical resource policies, every core function declaration, an alphabetical symbol index, and a glossary. You can read straight through or use the function reference beside an existing program.

Begin with the first-program chapter if the library is already installed. Read the rounding and error chapter before interpreting numerical return values. Read the memory and overlap chapter before replacing inputs in place. If a calculation returns an error, use the troubleshooting chapter and the numerical limits rather than assuming that more precision is always the remedy.

The source package includes the complete programs in examples/manual/. Short excerpts in the prose are teaching aids. Build and run the complete file when you want its full setup, checks, and cleanup. Each example has a named source file and an expected result that you can compare with your own run.

0.1 Scope and conventions

The qualified baseline is Linux x86-64 ELF with the LP64 data model and 64-bit GMP limbs. Linux under WSL follows that same target contract. Native Windows, macOS, ARM64, big-endian, and 32-bit targets require separate qualification. OpenMP and the MPFR adapter are optional. Portable-looking source code alone does not establish support for every platform on which it can be compiled.

The manual describes the governed core API and ABI epoch 1. The source package’s version macros and release record identify the particular library build. Precision is measured in bits unless decimal digits are stated explicitly. An equation describes an exact mathematical value; a stored ppf_t describes its finite binary representation. These are different objects, and much of reliable numerical programming consists of keeping the distinction visible.

The library has finite domain and resource policies. A successful certified path and a bounded numerical rejection are different outcomes. A complete API inventory is useful for navigation, but is not a whole-library formal proof. The numerical-limits appendix separates documented behavior from remaining review and boundary-evidence obligations.

0.2 License and attribution

The library and accompanying source are distributed under LGPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE.md, LICENSE, COPYING, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in the source package for the applicable terms and third-party notices. The release author uses the name Komorebi P.

1 Finding your way

Polyphase Float is a C library for binary floating-point arithmetic with a precision you choose for each number. It provides arithmetic, roots, mathematical constants and functions, conversions, and input/output through the ppf_t number type. A calculation can use more significand bits than the machine’s ordinary double, and it can choose how each result is rounded.

This book takes you from a working installation to calculations whose precision, ownership, and error handling you can explain. The first five chapters form a practical introduction. Later chapters develop the arithmetic families, numerical limits, interchange formats, and advanced interfaces. The reference entries are there when you need the exact declaration or contract of an individual function.

You do not need to understand the implementation’s multiplication algorithms to use the library. You do need to distinguish a number’s precision from its printed length, initialize and clear owned objects, and interpret return values correctly. Those three habits account for much of the introductory material.

1.1 Choose a reading route

Your starting point Suggested route
New to C numerical libraries Build and run the supplied example, read objects and contexts, then work through all four introductory programs.
Comfortable with C, new to arbitrary precision Read the precision discussion below and the rounding chapter before adapting the first program.
Moving from another multiprecision library Read ownership, explicit versus default contexts, return-value conventions, and the function reference for each migrated call.
Integrating an existing application Start with the installed CMake consumer, then review thread ownership, error handling, and the exact contracts of your operation families.
Investigating an unexpected answer Check the original input, destination precision, intermediate rounding, flags, and result category in that order.

The examples deliberately use small, inspectable calculations. Their simplicity makes API mistakes visible. Once those patterns are familiar, use the same initialization, return checking, and cleanup structure around a larger algorithm.

If you are reading a PDF, the source links identify complete files in the accompanying source tree. Commands run from the source directory unless a section explicitly changes directory. Shell prompts such as $ are omitted so that commands can be copied directly.

1.2 The four ideas behind a calculation

A typical operation combines four things:

  1. Operands contain the values already stored in the input objects.
  2. A destination supplies the precision of the result.
  3. A rounding mode chooses a representable answer when the exact result does not fit.
  4. A context supplies the exponent range, default policy, allocation callbacks, and diagnostic flags.

For example, ppf_mul(&result, &a, &b, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) multiplies the stored values of a and b, rounds into the existing precision of result, and uses ctx for the calculation. The & operator passes the address of an object. The first argument is the object to be written; the following number arguments are inputs.

An operand’s high precision does not automatically make the destination high precision. A 256-bit input multiplied into a 32-bit destination produces a 32-bit result. The context’s default precision does not resize an existing destination either. Choosing the destination is part of choosing the numerical calculation.

1.3 Bits, decimal digits, and magnitude

Precision is measured in binary significand bits. It describes the amount of significant binary information a regular value can hold, not the number of digits after the decimal point. The exponent controls magnitude separately. A very large value and a very small value can therefore use the same precision.

A useful conversion is

decimal-digit equivalent≈plog10(2), \text{decimal-digit equivalent} \approx p\log_{10}(2),

where pp is the number of significand bits.

Precision Approximate decimal-digit equivalent
24 bits 7.22
53 bits 15.95
80 bits 24.08
128 bits 38.53
256 bits 77.06

These are measures of storage resolution. They are not guarantees that an arbitrary calculation has that many correct decimal digits. Inaccurate input, cancellation, and an ill-conditioned problem can reduce the useful accuracy of a result.

To budget space for roughly dd decimal significant digits, start with ⌈dlog2(10)⌉\lceil d\log_2(10)\rceil bits, then allow additional working precision according to the algorithm. For example, 50 decimal digits correspond to about 167 bits before any allowance for intermediate error. There is no universal number of extra bits that makes every algorithm reliable.

Some values are exactly representable in a finite binary significand. One half is exact because it is a power of two. One tenth and one third have nonterminating binary expansions, so storing them at a finite precision generally involves rounding. Printing more decimal digits can reveal the stored approximation; it cannot create missing information.

The default precision is 53 bits. That familiar size does not make every aspect of the object model identical to a C double. Polyphase Float has its own exponent range, explicit rounding controls, flags, and special-value rules.

1.4 What the core depends on

The production core uses GMP for integer storage and arithmetic support. MPFR is optional: it supports an interoperability adapter and differential tests. You can build and use the core without an MPFR runtime dependency. The build chapter starts with that smaller configuration.

The supported baseline is Linux x86-64 with the LP64 data model and 64-bit GMP limbs. LP64 means that pointers and C long integers are 64 bits. Windows readers can follow the Linux workflow inside an x86-64 Ubuntu environment under WSL; native Windows toolchains are outside this baseline. The installation chapter makes the shell boundary explicit.

The public API includes finite-precision arithmetic and bounded algorithms. Some mathematical-function implementations can reject requests outside their practical limits or after a finite refinement budget. The relevant reference entries describe those limits and failure behavior. A wide representable exponent range does not imply that every mathematical function can successfully evaluate every representable argument.

1.5 Read results at three levels

When an operation finishes, ask three separate questions:

  • Did the operation report an unrecovered failure? Ternary-returning operations use PPF_TERNARY_ERROR for this purpose.
  • What kind of result was produced? A result may be regular, zero, infinity, or NaN.
  • What numerical diagnostics were raised? Context flags record conditions such as inexact rounding, overflow, or division by zero.

A nonzero ternary result is usually a rounding direction, not a failure. Conversely, a special value may be produced through the documented arithmetic rules without returning PPF_TERNARY_ERROR. The rounding chapter develops both distinctions with runnable examples.

The word exact also needs a reference point. If an input string has already been rounded into an eight-bit object, copying that stored value to a 128-bit object may be exact. The copy still contains the original eight-bit approximation. Exactness of one operation does not recover information lost earlier.

1.6 A small vocabulary

A significand carries the significant digits of a number; an exponent scales that significand by a power of the radix. The radix is the numeral-system base, such as two or ten. A destination is the initialized object an operation writes. A rounding mode chooses among nearby representable results. A ternary result describes whether the stored result is below, equal to, or above the exact result of the operation. A sticky flag remains set until explicitly cleared or restored. An owned object is responsible for storage that must eventually be released.

These terms recur because they describe different responsibilities. Precision belongs to a number; flags belong to a context; storage belongs to an owner; and mathematical accuracy belongs to the complete calculation.

1.7 Before moving on

You are ready to begin when you can identify the source directory, choose a Linux build environment, and set aside a separate build directory. In the next chapter you will compile the library, run an example, and link a small application against an installed package. You can return to the numerical discussion after seeing that first program run.

Check your understanding. Does requesting 40 decimal digits of printed output make a 53-bit number more precise?

Answer. No. It changes the text representation. To retain more information, initialize the destination at a higher binary precision and compute or parse the value at that precision. Widening an existing approximation alone does not recover its discarded information.

2 Building, installing, and linking

The goal of this chapter is a working C program linked to Polyphase Float. Start with the serial core, verify it, and add optional facilities when your application needs them. Keep the source, build output, and installation prefix separate: that makes it easier to repeat a build or diagnose which library an application is using.

A source directory contains CMakeLists.txt, include/, and src/. A build directory contains generated files and compiled binaries. An installation prefix is the destination tree from which another project consumes the headers, libraries, and CMake package. Building does not automatically install the library.

2.1 Prepare the system

The supported baseline is Linux x86-64 ELF, using LP64 and 64-bit GMP limbs. You need:

Component Purpose
C11 compiler, such as GCC or Clang Compile the library and application
CMake 3.23 or newer Configure, build, test, and install
Make or Ninja Execute the generated build rules
Official GMP development headers and library Build the core arithmetic library
POSIX threads and the platform math library Provide system facilities used by the core
Python 3 Run source audits and Python-based tests

MPFR development files are optional for ordinary core use and required for the full differential-test and adapter route described below. A development package includes headers as well as a linkable library. Having only a runtime shared library is insufficient for a normal development installation.

On an Ubuntu system with package access, the following installs the basic development tools:

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential cmake libgmp-dev pkg-config python3

Check the installed tools before configuring:

cc --version
cmake --version
python3 --version

Use your distribution’s supported package sources. Package versions differ by distribution release; the CMake version must meet the minimum above. The Ubuntu package index documents the packages available for each release.

2.1.1 Windows: enter the Linux environment first

On a supported Windows installation, open PowerShell as an administrator and run:

wsl --install

Follow the restart and Ubuntu first-run prompts, including creation of a Linux user account. Microsoft maintains the WSL installation instructions, including routes for systems that need additional setup. This bootstrap normally downloads components and is separate from building Polyphase Float.

After Ubuntu opens, run the Linux commands in this chapter inside Ubuntu, not in PowerShell. Use an x86-64 Linux environment and keep the project in its Linux home directory. This is a Linux build on a Windows host; it does not provide a native Windows DLL or establish support for an ARM machine. Verify the build and tests in your own WSL environment as you would on any other Linux installation.

2.1.2 Preparing an offline build

The core build does not need to fetch a dependency from the network once the source archive, compiler, CMake, build tool, and GMP development files are present. Arrange those prerequisites before disconnecting. On a managed offline system, obtain the matching distribution packages and their dependencies through your administrator or an approved package cache. Copying only libgmp.so from another machine does not supply the headers or ensure an ABI-compatible development environment.

The package-install commands above require access to configured package repositories unless the necessary packages are already cached. They are preparation commands, not a promise of an offline package installation. After preparation, unpack the complete source archive into a writable directory and run the following build commands there.

2.2 Build and run the core

From the directory containing CMakeLists.txt:

cmake -S . -B build/release \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DPPF_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DPPF_MPFR_SUPPORT=OFF \
  -DPPF_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/release -j2
./build/release/example_basic
ctest --test-dir build/release --output-on-failure -j1

The trailing backslash continues a shell command on the next line; do not put characters after it. -S . selects the current source directory. -B build/release selects a separate build directory. -j2 permits two build jobs; reduce it to -j1 on a memory-constrained machine. The test command uses one test job to make failures easier to follow.

The basic example prints:

x (256 bits) = 3.10000e1
y (80 bits)  = 3.10000e1

Both objects contain the integer 31 exactly. Their different precisions show that storage precision can differ without changing an exactly representable value. The file examples/basic.c includes checked initialization, calculation, output, and cleanup.

This configuration builds the core without MPFR or an OpenMP runtime requirement. Both shared and static core libraries are enabled by default. The tests available in a configured build depend on its capabilities; a core-only test run is useful local validation, but it is not the full MPFR-enabled differential matrix.

If configuration fails, fix that error before running the build command. If compilation fails, read the first compiler error before later messages caused by it. A successful cmake configuration alone does not mean the library has compiled or its tests have run.

2.3 Install to your user account

A user-local installation avoids requiring administrator privileges:

cmake --install build/release --prefix "$HOME/.local"

The prefix contains headers, libraries, package metadata, and documentation. Depending on the platform’s installation conventions, the library directory can be lib or a nested directory such as lib/x86_64-linux-gnu. Use the exported CMake package instead of assuming that directory name in application build scripts.

Verify consumption from the installation, rather than accidentally linking back to the source build:

cmake -S tests/install_consumer -B build/install-consumer \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$HOME/.local" \
  -DPPF_CONSUMER_COMPONENTS=core
cmake --build build/install-consumer -j2
ctest --test-dir build/install-consumer --output-on-failure

CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH tells CMake where to search for installed packages. It does not modify the system package manager. If you maintain several Polyphase Float installations, choose one prefix deliberately and use a fresh consumer build directory when switching between them.

2.4 Create your own CMake application

Make an application directory alongside the library source directory. Place a copy of intro_first.c in it as main.c, and add this CMakeLists.txt:

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.23)
project(my_calculation LANGUAGES C)

find_package(PolyphaseFloat CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS core)
add_executable(my_calculation main.c)
target_compile_features(my_calculation PRIVATE c_std_11)
set_target_properties(my_calculation PROPERTIES C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
target_link_libraries(my_calculation PRIVATE PolyphaseFloat::shared)

From that application directory:

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$HOME/.local"
cmake --build build -j2
./build/my_calculation

Expected output is 2 * 3 = 6.00000e0. The imported target supplies the library’s include paths and transitive link requirements. You do not need to copy headers into the application or hand-maintain GMP and thread link flags in this CMake project.

To select the installed static core, replace PolyphaseFloat::shared with PolyphaseFloat::static, provided that form was built and installed. Static linking still needs the relevant dependency libraries; the imported target expresses those requirements. The word static does not imply that every dependency in the final executable is statically linked.

COMPONENTS core makes the dependency choice explicit. An application using the optional MPFR adapter should request the mpfr component and use its documented adapter target. The independent core has no need for that component.

2.5 Compile the introductory programs directly

For a quick experiment with the serial build above, run this from the library source directory:

cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic \
  -Iinclude examples/manual/intro_first.c \
  build/release/libpolyphase_float.a \
  -lgmp -lm -pthread -o build/release/intro_first
./build/release/intro_first

The source comes before the static library, and the dependency libraries follow it. That order matters to ordinary static linking. -Iinclude locates the public header; it does not locate the compiled library. For the other introductory programs, replace intro_first in both the source path and executable name.

This command is intentionally tied to the serial build in this chapter. An OpenMP-enabled static build can require additional compiler and runtime flags. For a maintained application, prefer the CMake imported target so that the selected build’s dependencies travel with it.

2.6 Add optional capabilities deliberately

Use a new build directory for a different compiler, sanitizer, or major configuration. CMake caches detected paths and compiler properties; reusing a directory after changing toolchains can produce confusing combinations.

For full differential testing on Ubuntu, first install official MPFR development files:

sudo apt-get install libmpfr-dev

Then configure a separate validation build:

cmake -S . -B build/validation \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
  -DPPF_OPENMP=AUTO \
  -DPPF_MPFR_SUPPORT=ON \
  -DPPF_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON \
  -DPPF_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build/validation -j2
ctest --test-dir build/validation --output-on-failure -j1

AUTO enables OpenMP when the compiler probe succeeds; ON requires it; OFF excludes it. For MPFR, ON requires support and OFF selects the independent core. Use official MPFR headers when installing the adapter. A compatibility-header validation route does not provide the same installable adapter configuration.

Native CPU tuning is off by default. Keep it off when distributing a binary to machines with potentially different instruction sets. The complete option list, packaging staging commands, and tooling configurations are in Building Polyphase Float (docs/BUILDING.md); the test labels and qualification boundaries are in Testing (docs/TESTING.md).

2.7 Diagnose the first failure

Symptom First action
cmake is not found or is too old Install a suitable CMake package and check cmake --version.
GMP headers or library cannot be found Install the development package; check that headers and library target the same architecture.
PolyphaseFloatConfig.cmake cannot be found Install the library, then pass its prefix through CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH.
The compiler cannot find polyphase_float.h Use the imported CMake target, or check -Iinclude and your current directory.
The linker reports undefined ppf_ symbols Confirm that the library is linked and matches the header; for direct static linking, check argument order.
The executable cannot load a shared library Check the installation prefix and runtime library search configuration; do not substitute an unrelated shared object.
A test fails Keep the --output-on-failure output and record compiler, configuration, and platform before changing settings.

A useful problem report includes the first failing command, its full error message, the configured options, compiler version, and whether the failure occurs during configuration, compilation, linking, execution, or testing. Those stages have different remedies.

Exercise. Why can #include "polyphase_float.h" compile successfully while the final link fails?

Answer. The header provides declarations to the compiler. The linker still needs the compiled implementations and their dependencies. Linking PolyphaseFloat::shared or PolyphaseFloat::static through CMake supplies that second part.

3 Numbers, contexts, and ownership

A ppf_t is an owned numerical object, not a plain scalar that you can copy with C assignment. A ppf_context_t carries the policy and temporary resources used by operations. Keeping their roles separate makes a program easier to reason about: numbers retain values, while contexts govern how calculations are performed and record what happened.

This chapter uses explicit contexts throughout. That makes the source of precision policy, range limits, flags, and allocations visible at each call site. The thread-local convenience interface is useful too, but mixing the two styles casually is a common source of misleading diagnostics.

3.1 Start with a complete lifetime

A normal object passes through four stages: declare its structure, initialize its storage, assign or calculate a value, and clear it. Here is the pattern in a small scope:

ppf_context_t ctx;
ppf_t x = {0};
int status = 1;

if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
if (ppf_init2_ctx(&x, 128, &ctx) != 0) goto cleanup;
if (ppf_set_ui(&x, 7, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
    goto cleanup;
status = 0;

cleanup:
ppf_clear(&x);
ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
return status;

This is a function-body pattern, not a complete translation unit. The first-programs chapter includes the header, main, checked output, and thread cleanup in complete programs.

ppf_t x = {0} zero-initializes the C structure so a common cleanup path can safely clear it even if initialization did not complete. It does not create a numerical zero or a valid initialized number. Only after successful ppf_init2_ctx may ordinary numerical operations use the object.

Successful initialization gives the object its storage and precision and leaves its value as NaN. Assign the intended value before using it as an operand. To make a numerical zero, call ppf_set_zero(&x, 1) on an initialized object; the positive sign argument selects positive zero.

If allocating significand storage fails, ppf_init2_ctx returns failure and leaves an all-zero structure. Starting from {0} also handles early argument validation failures safely. Check the return before proceeding. A nonzero initialization status is not a rounding direction.

The goto cleanup statements provide one release path. They do not jump back into a partially initialized calculation. For a C program that owns several resources, this structure keeps an early failure from bypassing cleanup. Clear each object you successfully initialized, and avoid reinitializing an object whose previous storage is still live.

3.2 Read an operation declaration

Consider the multiplication interface:

int ppf_mul(ppf_t *rop, const ppf_t *a, const ppf_t *b,
            ppf_rnd_t rnd, ppf_context_t *ctx);

rop is the result operand, or destination. The const qualification on a and b marks them as input pointers; any permitted overlap with the destination follows the aliasing rules discussed below. rnd selects rounding, and ctx supplies execution policy and flags. The returned integer is a ternary result, whose interpretation is explained in the next chapter.

In a call such as ppf_mul(&product, &a, &b, PPF_RNDN, &ctx), each & supplies an address. The function writes through the destination pointer. There is no C expression product = a * b for these objects: C’s built-in multiplication operator does not know the library’s ownership and rounding rules.

Library functions differ in return conventions. Read the declaration and reference entry instead of treating every int as the same kind of answer. Initialization returns a status; multiplication returns a ternary; comparison returns an ordering result; a predicate answers a yes/no question. They can all use the C type int while meaning different things.

3.3 Precision belongs to the object

ppf_init2_ctx(&x, 128, &ctx) explicitly creates a 128-bit destination. Use ppf_get_prec(&x) to inspect that precision. The minimum supported precision is two bits; the maximum practical request also depends on storage and implementation limits. Choose a precision for the numerical work, rather than allocating the largest value the type could express.

Different precision-changing functions have deliberately different purposes:

Function Effect
ppf_reserve Ensures storage capacity without changing the declared precision or numerical value.
ppf_set_prec Changes the precision and discards the previous value, leaving NaN on success.
ppf_prec_round Changes precision while rounding the current value under the supplied mode and context.
ppf_context_set_default_precision Changes a context’s default policy; existing objects retain their precisions.

Use ppf_prec_round when the existing value must be retained. Narrowing can lose information. Widening can preserve the stored value exactly when it remains within the applicable range, but cannot reconstruct digits lost before the widening. Always check the return value; a request for more precision can require allocation.

Initialization offers several precision and context choices. ppf_init uses the calling thread’s default context and its default precision. ppf_init2 uses an explicit precision with that thread’s default context. ppf_init2_ctx uses the precision you pass and the explicit context you pass. Setting an explicit context’s default precision does not redirect a later ppf_init to that context. For introductory code, a named precision and ppf_init2_ctx make the intended pairing unambiguous.

A higher-precision source does not resize a lower-precision destination during ppf_set or arithmetic. That behavior lets you design a calculation with high-precision intermediate work and a deliberately smaller final output. It also means that a mistakenly small temporary can lose information before the final output is computed.

3.4 Copy values without copying ownership

C structure assignment copies pointers. Consequently, b = a and memcpy(&b, &a, sizeof b) are not ways to duplicate an owned Polyphase Float number. They can make two structures refer to the same storage and later free that storage twice.

Instead, initialize b at its intended precision and call:

int ternary = ppf_set(&b, &a, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);

This copies the numerical value into b with the destination’s rounding and precision. The allocations remain independently owned. Check PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before interpreting the sign of ternary.

ppf_swap(&a, &b) exchanges the complete object states, including precision and ownership. It is useful when an algorithm wants to make a completed temporary become the current result. After a swap, each variable owns the state it received and should still be cleared exactly once. Do not assume that either variable retained its old precision.

Pass object pointers to your own helper functions too. A helper can receive ppf_t *out and const ppf_t *input; taking a ppf_t by value would copy its owning fields. Keep helpers’ ownership contracts simple: either they operate on an already initialized destination, or they explicitly initialize a new one and document who clears it.

Aliasing means that two arguments refer to the same object or overlapping storage. Some operations support using an input as the destination; others have stricter rules, especially paired outputs and batch interfaces. The introductory programs use separate objects so their data flow is visible. Check the per-function aliasing contract before replacing those objects with an in-place optimization.

3.5 Give each context a clear owner

A context holds default precision, default rounding, the minimum and maximum exponent, sticky flags, allocation callbacks, and reusable temporary storage. Initialize it with ppf_context_init, then adjust policy through the public setters if necessary. ppf_context_set_rounding accepts a concrete rounding mode; operations can subsequently request that policy using PPF_RND_DEFAULT.

A context is mutable even when the operation’s mathematical inputs are read-only: allocation and flags can change it. In concurrent code, give each worker its own context or protect shared use with appropriate synchronization. A shared read-only operand is permitted while no thread mutates, clears, resizes, swaps, or reinitializes it. A destination requires exclusive access for the duration of an operation. OpenMP support inside the library does not remove these application ownership rules.

Use ppf_context_clone to create a separate context with copied policy and flags. It initializes independent temporary-storage state rather than sharing the source context’s active scratch arena. The clone retains the allocator callbacks and opaque state, so a custom allocator’s lifetime and thread-safety requirements still apply. The destination of cloning must be available for initialization; do not clone over a live context without first releasing it.

For ordinary code, clear numbers before clearing the context that created them. Each number actually retains the allocator callbacks needed to free its own allocation, so the context structure itself is not a hidden owner of every number. With custom allocators, however, the opaque allocator state must stay valid until all dependent objects, buffers, and contexts have been released. The straightforward object-first cleanup order makes that obligation easy to meet.

3.6 Use the matching release function

Resource How it is released
Initialized, normally owned ppf_t ppf_clear
Explicit ppf_context_t ppf_context_clear
String allocated by ppf_get_str(NULL, ...) ppf_free_str
Successful ppf_asprintf or ppf_vasprintf output C free
Caller-supplied output buffer Its existing application owner releases it

Those string rules are different on purpose. Do not infer the deallocator merely from the return type char *. The API reference states ownership for each allocating function. The introductory examples use stream output so there is no returned string allocation to manage.

ppf_thread_cleanup releases the calling thread’s default context and internal thread-local workspaces. It may be called repeatedly. It does not clear your user-owned numbers, explicit contexts, plans, or random states. Call it after releasing those resources at the end of a worker or a standalone program when deterministic thread cleanup is desired. Normal thread-exit cleanup is also available where the library successfully registers its POSIX cleanup key; explicit cleanup keeps the example’s lifetime visible.

3.7 Keep explicit and default diagnostics together

If a calculation receives &ctx, inspect it with ppf_context_flags(&ctx) and clear it with ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, mask). The shorter ppf_flags_* functions refer to the calling thread’s default context. They do not automatically inspect whichever explicit context your previous operation used.

Many numerical APIs resolve a null context to the thread-local default context, but lifecycle calls have their own preconditions. Do not generalize the null-context convention to every function. The explicit form used here avoids that ambiguity and works naturally when a program manages multiple numerical policies.

Exercise. An eight-bit object contains an approximation to 0.1. Which operation lets you increase its precision while retaining its stored value: ppf_set_prec or ppf_prec_round?

Answer. ppf_prec_round, with appropriate range and rounding policy. The widened object still contains the earlier approximation. ppf_set_prec discards the value and leaves NaN on success. Parsing the original decimal string again into a wider object is a different operation and can recover more information from that original input.

Exercise. Can clearing a context replace clearing all numbers created through it?

Answer. No. Numbers own their significand allocations. Clear each owned number and then clear the context’s own resources. The same distinction applies to thread cleanup.

4 Rounding, flags, and exceptional results

A floating-point calculation produces a stored value and information about how that value was obtained. Polyphase Float exposes that information through rounding modes, ternary return values, result categories, and context flags. These mechanisms answer different questions. Using them together makes it possible to distinguish an ordinary rounded answer from an invalid request, an exceptional mathematical result, or a practical implementation limit.

For a first program, use nearest rounding, check the failure sentinel, and inspect any result categories your application cannot accept. Add flag handling according to the calculation’s needs. Inexact rounding is expected for many useful calculations; treating it as a program failure would reject values such as one third at every finite binary precision.

4.1 Choose a rounding direction

Imagine the exact real result between two adjacent representable values at the destination precision. A rounding mode decides which value is stored.

Mode Meaning
PPF_RNDN Nearest; an exact halfway case selects the even significand.
PPF_RNDZ Toward zero.
PPF_RNDU Toward positive infinity.
PPF_RNDD Toward negative infinity.
PPF_RNDA Away from zero.
PPF_RNDF Faithful rounding: an allowed adjacent representable result.
PPF_RND_DEFAULT For context-based numerical operations, use the resolved context’s default rounding mode.

The words up and down refer to numerical order, not magnitude. For a negative result, rounding toward positive infinity makes the answer less negative; rounding toward negative infinity makes it more negative. Rounding toward zero agrees with downward rounding for positive results and upward rounding for negative results.

For nearest-even, “even” refers to the least significant retained significand bit, not the last decimal digit in a printed string. Halfway decisions therefore depend on the binary representation at the destination precision.

Faithful rounding does not request a unique nearest result in every case. Do not use it when your algorithm requires a specifically directed bound or a particular nearest-even bit pattern. The function’s own contract describes its supported settlement and reporting behavior. For introductory calculations, PPF_RNDN, PPF_RNDD, and PPF_RNDU make the intent particularly easy to inspect.

Passing a concrete mode on a call makes that choice independent of later changes to the context default. Passing PPF_RND_DEFAULT is useful when a whole operation sequence deliberately follows a policy selected by the caller.

Check the individual contract before passing PPF_RND_DEFAULT to other interfaces. Rounding-policy setters and ppf_can_round require concrete modes. The ppf_fits_*_p predicates use a fresh private context, so their default is nearest-even rather than the calling thread’s policy. The naming helpers inspect the enumeration: ppf_rounding_name returns the name "PPF_RND_DEFAULT", while ppf_print_rnd_mode returns NULL for that value.

4.2 Check the failure sentinel before the sign

Many assignment and arithmetic functions return a ternary integer. For an ordinary finite rounding result:

Return relation Interpretation
Negative The stored result is below the exact result.
Zero The stored result equals the exact result.
Positive The stored result is above the exact result.

There is also a separate sentinel, PPF_TERNARY_ERROR, for an unrecovered failure. That sentinel is a negative integer. Testing t < 0 before excluding it would misclassify failure as a valid result rounded downward.

Use this order:

int t = ppf_div(&result, &numerator, &denominator,
                PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
if (t == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) {
    /* Handle the failure; do not interpret t as a direction. */
} else if (t < 0) {
    /* The ordinary finite result is below its exact target. */
} else if (t > 0) {
    /* The ordinary finite result is above its exact target. */
} else {
    /* No inexact direction is reported; also check result category. */
}

Use the sign of a non-error ternary, not an assumption that the library will always return exactly -1 or +1. Also do not replace the error check with if (t != 0): that would classify successful inexact results as failures.

The exact target is the mathematical operation on the values actually stored in the operands. If a decimal input was rounded earlier, a later zero ternary says nothing about whether that input was the intended decimal real number. This distinction is especially important when an operation subtracts nearly equal approximations: the subtraction can be exact while the result has poor accuracy relative to the original problem.

Special values require their documented category rules rather than an ordinary finite ordering interpretation. For example, division by zero can produce infinity, and an invalid arithmetic combination can produce NaN. A zero return alone is not a general certificate that the result is a finite exact real value.

4.3 Different functions return different kinds of answers

The C type of a return value is not enough to interpret it correctly.

Example Return convention
ppf_init2_ctx, ppf_context_init Status: zero on success, failure otherwise.
ppf_set, ppf_set_ui, ppf_mul, ppf_div Ternary, with PPF_TERNARY_ERROR checked first.
ppf_set_str Status: zero for an accepted complete input, -1 on failure.
ppf_strtofr Ternary plus an end pointer used to inspect parsing progress.
ppf_out_str Output count; zero indicates failure.
ppf_cmp Comparison result, subject to its special-value rules.
ppf_nan_p, ppf_zero_p Predicates: nonzero means the condition holds.

In particular, a successful ppf_set_str call can involve rounding even though its return is zero. That API reports acceptance of the string, not a ternary direction. If you need parsing progress or rounding direction, use the appropriate parsing interface and validate its end pointer as described in the input/output chapter.

Do not build a helper that treats all functions with return type int identically. A useful application helper can be specific: one helper for status-returning setup, another for ternary arithmetic, and a separate policy for exceptional numerical categories.

4.4 Observe sticky flags

A context accumulates diagnostic flags. “Sticky” means that a later successful or exact operation does not automatically erase a flag set by an earlier operation. This allows a program to examine whether any step in a sequence encountered a condition.

Flag General meaning
PPF_FLAG_INEXACT A result required inexact rounding.
PPF_FLAG_UNDERFLOW An operation encountered its underflow condition.
PPF_FLAG_OVERFLOW An operation encountered its overflow condition.
PPF_FLAG_DIVBY0 A division-by-zero condition was reported.
PPF_FLAG_NAN A NaN-related or invalid arithmetic condition was reported.
PPF_FLAG_ERANGE An invalid, out-of-range, or otherwise rejected request was reported.
PPF_FLAG_ALLOC A configured project allocator rejected an allocation request.

These descriptions introduce the flags; individual operation contracts specify their exact triggering rules. For example, exponent-range operations and subnormalization have their own defined underflow semantics. Do not infer every function’s behavior from a hardware floating-point exception model.

To isolate one operation, clear the flags you intend to monitor before it, then save the resulting flags immediately afterward:

ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
int t = ppf_div(&result, &one, &three, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
ppf_flags_t observed = ppf_context_flags(&ctx);

Check t before using the numerical result. The saved observed value describes the context state at that point. Subsequent conversions or other numerical work may alter the live flags, so saving them before formatting diagnostics avoids accidentally attributing later events to the division.

If an application wants flags for an entire algorithm, clear them once at the algorithm boundary and inspect them at the end. Clearing after every call would lose that accumulated record. If you need both an outer accumulated record and a local observation, use the save/restore interfaces with a deliberate mask and combine the observations according to your application’s policy.

An allocation flag does not always mean the calculation ultimately failed. Some operations can recover through an exact fallback after an optional allocation fails, leaving the flag set as a diagnostic. Check the operation’s return and result as well as the flag. The allocation contract covers project-controlled paths; GMP, libc, and operating-system allocation behavior are separate domains.

4.5 Recognize special values

Polyphase Float distinguishes regular finite nonzero values, signed zeros, signed infinities, and NaNs. Use predicates such as ppf_regular_p, ppf_zero_p, ppf_inf_p, and ppf_nan_p instead of inspecting internal fields or relying on text formatting.

A numerical zero is finite, but it is not a regular value in this category terminology. Thus ppf_regular_p alone is not a test accepting every finite number. If your application accepts ordinary finite values including zero, accept regular values or zeros and reject the other categories.

Positive and negative zero compare as equal numerical zeros, but their signs can matter for sign-sensitive operations. ppf_signbit lets you inspect the retained sign. NaN is not an ordinary ordered number: comparisons involving it need the documented predicate or ordering behavior. Classify a value before using it in a policy that assumes an ordinary finite order.

The introductory flag program demonstrates two different exceptional operations. Dividing positive one by positive zero produces positive infinity and sets DIVBY0. Dividing zero by zero produces NaN and sets NAN. Neither case should be silently treated as an ordinary finite answer, even if the API follows its special-value rule without returning the failure sentinel.

An application decides whether infinity or NaN is acceptable. A scientific routine may propagate them with diagnostics; a file-format validator may reject them at input; an optimization algorithm may treat them as a failed candidate. Make that policy explicit at the boundary where the value enters the application.

4.6 Understand exponent range separately from precision

Precision determines significand resolution. The context’s emin and emax limit the exponent range used by operations. Increasing precision does not necessarily fix an overflow caused by a restrictive exponent range, and widening the exponent range does not restore precision lost through rounding.

Regular values are normalized; the object model does not store an implicit ladder of subnormal values beneath the minimum normal value. Ordinary range settlement below that boundary chooses signed zero or the minimum normal value according to the applicable rounding rule. Overflow chooses infinity or the largest finite value according to sign and rounding. Advanced range and subnormalization APIs expose additional operations with specific contracts.

For most first programs, retain the default range. If your application changes it, do so deliberately and check the status returned by ppf_context_set_range. Existing objects are not automatically recomputed just because policy changes. A subsequent assignment or operation can settle a result under the new range.

4.7 Separate recoverable diagnostics from failed computation

A successful rounded result may be entirely suitable for an application. An unrecovered failure needs an explicit path: return an application error, select a documented alternative, or retry with a justified change of parameters. Do not print the destination as though it were newly valid merely because it still contains something.

Destination preservation depends on the kind of failure and the function’s contract. Covered project-allocation failures preserve an initialized destination. Exhaustion of a mathematical function’s numerical refinement budget can instead publish NaN with ERANGE and PPF_TERNARY_ERROR. Invalid input and resource-limit rejection also have operation-specific rules. Consult the relevant reference entry before relying on an old value after a failed call.

Increasing precision is not a universal remedy for rejection: a request can exceed a domain bound, an iteration budget, or a resource policy. Capture the arguments, precision, rounding mode, relevant flags, and result category when diagnosing such a case. That record is more informative than a decimal answer alone.

Exercise. An operation returns a negative integer. What must you test before describing the answer as rounded downward?

Answer. Test whether it equals PPF_TERNARY_ERROR. If it does, it is failure. If it does not, interpret the ternary sign under the operation’s ordinary-result contract and inspect any special category relevant to the application.

Exercise. An inexact division is followed by an exact assignment, and INEXACT remains set. Did the assignment fail?

Answer. No such conclusion follows. The flag is sticky. The division may have set it, and the assignment does not clear it. To diagnose the assignment alone, clear the monitored flags before the assignment or use an explicit save/restore policy.

5 First complete programs

The four programs in this chapter turn the preceding concepts into code you can compile and inspect. Each is a complete C11 program with deterministic output. Each checks its own expected numerical relationships and returns a nonzero process status if setup, calculation, verification, or output fails. Their shared structure is intentional: learning one cleanup and error-checking pattern gives you a foundation for a larger application.

The complete source files are in examples/manual. The build chapter gives a direct compiler command for the serial core. With examples and tests enabled, CMake also provides a target and a test for each program:

Source file Build target Main lesson
intro_first.c example_manual_intro_first A complete checked calculation
intro_rounding.c example_manual_intro_rounding Directed and nearest rounding
intro_flags.c example_manual_intro_flags Sticky flags and special values
intro_precision.c example_manual_intro_precision Widening versus recomputing

For example, from the source directory after configuring build/release:

cmake --build build/release --target example_manual_intro_first -j2
./build/release/example_manual_intro_first
ctest --test-dir build/release -L manual --output-on-failure

The manual label selects the manual examples registered in that build. The example results (docs/manual/EXAMPLE_RESULTS.md) describe their verification scope. These small demonstrations check their stated behavior; they are not a substitute for the full library test suite or validation of an application’s numerical algorithm.

5.1 Program 1: multiply two exact integers

Complete source: intro_first.c.

The program computes two times three in a 128-bit destination. Small integers make the arithmetic exact, so any discrepancy points to setup, usage, or execution rather than a subtle decimal approximation.

#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t a = {0}, b = {0}, product = {0};
    int status = 1;
    int ternary;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) {
        fputs("Cannot initialize the context.\n", stderr);
        return 1;
    }
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&a, 128, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&b, 128, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&product, 128, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_set_ui(&a, 2, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR ||
        ppf_set_ui(&b, 3, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;

    ternary = ppf_mul(&product, &a, &b, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    if (ternary != 0 || ppf_cmp_ui(&product, 6, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (fputs("2 * 3 = ", stdout) == EOF ||
        ppf_out_str(stdout, 10, 6, &product, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0 ||
        fputc('\n', stdout) == EOF || fflush(stdout) == EOF)
        goto cleanup;
    status = 0;

cleanup:
    if (status != 0) fputs("The calculation or output failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&product);
    ppf_clear(&b);
    ppf_clear(&a);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

Expected output:

2 * 3 = 6.00000e0

The ui in ppf_set_ui denotes an unsigned C integer input. Both input assignments are exact at this precision. Multiplication returns zero because six is exactly representable. The program then checks the numerical answer using ppf_cmp_ui, rather than trusting that a successful call necessarily matches its intended example.

ppf_out_str(stdout, 10, 6, ...) prints in base ten with six significant digits. The e0 exponent means multiplication by ten to the zeroth power. The output precision of six digits is a display choice; the destination still has 128 binary bits of precision.

The example checks both library output and the surrounding C stream operations. A calculation can succeed while writing its answer fails. fflush makes a pending buffered output failure visible before the program reports success.

For a C beginner, the || operators in setup are short-circuit tests: once one condition reports failure, later initializations in that expression are skipped and execution goes to cleanup. Because all object structures started at {0}, clearing the remaining structures is safe. status stays one until every required step succeeds.

5.2 Program 2: see where one third lands

Complete source: intro_rounding.c.

This program stores one and three exactly, then divides them into three eight-bit destinations. The central calls are:

down = ppf_div(&lower, &one, &three, PPF_RNDD, &ctx);
near = ppf_div(&nearest, &one, &three, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
up = ppf_div(&upper, &one, &three, PPF_RNDU, &ctx);

The complete program checks every failure sentinel before inspecting the signs. It also verifies that the lower result is smaller than the upper result and that the nearest result equals the upper result in this particular example.

Expected output:

down    = 3.32031250e-1 (below)
nearest = 3.33984375e-1 (above)
up      = 3.33984375e-1 (above)

At eight-bit precision, the adjacent representable values around one third are

L=170512=0.33203125,U=171512=0.333984375. L=\frac{170}{512}=0.33203125, \qquad U=\frac{171}{512}=0.333984375.

Their distances from one third are 1/7681/768 and 1/15361/1536, respectively. The upper neighbor is closer, so nearest rounding chooses it. This is not a halfway case. The directed results bracket the exact quotient of the stored inputs, which are exactly one and three.

The program prints nine decimal significant digits so these particular binary values can be read clearly. It does not require nine accurate decimal digits in the quotient: eight binary bits have much coarser resolution. Here the extra printed digits expose the exact small dyadic values being stored.

Directed rounding is a tool for constructing bounds, but a complete interval algorithm must account for every operation and the uncertainty in its inputs. Running the last step once downward and once upward does not automatically enclose a mathematical expression whose earlier steps were rounded without bounds.

Try it. Increase all five object precisions from eight to sixteen. The printed endpoints should get closer, but the existing assertions about which endpoint is nearest are specific to the original example and must be reconsidered. When exploring, compare numerical relationships and ternary directions; do not simply change expected output until a test passes.

5.3 Program 3: distinguish flags from return values

Complete source: intro_flags.c.

This program performs a sequence whose diagnostic state is easy to predict. It begins with eight-bit one third, performs an exact assignment, clears flags, and then evaluates two exceptional divisions.

Expected output:

1 / 3: INEXACT is set
exact assignment: INEXACT is still set
after clearing: no flags are set
1 / 0: positive infinity; DIVBY0 is set
0 / 0: NaN; NAN is set

The exact assignment is two. Its zero ternary does not erase the earlier INEXACT flag. The program explicitly checks both facts: assignment was exact, and the previous flag remains. It then calls ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL) to start a fresh observation period.

For the exceptional divisions, the code checks the failure sentinel, saves the flags, and inspects the result category. It requires positive infinity after one divided by positive zero, and NaN after zero divided by zero. The output text describes those verified conditions; it does not claim that every other possible flag bit is absent.

This is a useful pattern for an application boundary. Decide which categories and flags are acceptable for the task, then test them explicitly. A calculation intended to produce an ordinary finite measurement may reject both infinities and NaNs. A diagnostic tool can display them and their causes. Both policies can use the same library operations.

Try it. Remove the flag-clear call immediately before the final zero-over-zero division. The previous DIVBY0 condition will remain in the context together with the newly reported NaN condition. That demonstrates why a flag set is a history since the last clear, not an automatic description of only the most recent call. Restore the clear afterward to retain the original example’s intended observation periods.

5.4 Program 4: widening does not restore lost input

Complete source: intro_precision.c.

This program compares three objects: a decimal string parsed at eight bits, an exact copy of that stored approximation into 128 bits, and the original string parsed directly at 128 bits.

if (ppf_set_str(&coarse, "0.1", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0 ||
    ppf_set_str(&fresh, "0.1", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0)
    goto cleanup;
ternary = ppf_set(&widened, &coarse, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);

Notice the two return conventions. ppf_set_str returns a status, so nonzero is failure. ppf_set returns a ternary, so the complete source checks PPF_TERNARY_ERROR first and then verifies that this widening copy is exact.

Expected output:

parsed at 8 bits     = 1.00097656250e-1
copied to 128 bits   = 1.00097656250e-1
parsed at 128 bits   = 1.00000000000e-1
changing the default leaves existing precisions unchanged

The first two objects are numerically equal. The wider copy has room for more bits, but the copy operation receives only the value already stored in coarse. The direct 128-bit parse receives the original decimal input and therefore produces a different, much closer approximation to one tenth. Its displayed twelve digits do not imply that binary one tenth has become exact.

The program also sets the explicit context’s default precision to 256 and verifies that existing objects retain their eight-bit and 128-bit precisions. Policy changes do not silently rewrite previously created numbers.

For decimal data, parsing a decimal string directly avoids an intermediate conversion through a C double. In contrast, ppf_set_d(&x, 0.1, ...) receives the binary value of the C literal after the compiler has represented it as a double. A wider destination can preserve that input faithfully but cannot recover the decimal value the literal was intended to suggest. Neither route invents information absent from the input; choose the route that represents your actual data source.

5.5 Adapt the pattern to an application

Before replacing these small calculations with a larger formula, write down the precision of each input, temporary, and final destination. Decide how input is obtained, which rounding modes are required, and which exceptional categories the caller accepts. Place flag-clearing boundaries where they correspond to meaningful units of work.

Keep the numerical operation separate from presentation. A useful calculation helper accepts initialized objects and a context, performs the work, and reports a checked result. The caller decides how many digits to print and where to send them. That separation makes it easier to test numerical relationships without depending on a particular output format.

Finally, keep a meaningful check. Exact small cases, symmetries, independently computed bounds, and comparisons at higher working precision can all be useful, provided you understand what they establish. Repeating one algorithm at more bits is a diagnostic technique, not automatically a proof of the final digits. The later numerical chapters explain the stronger tools available for specific operation families.

Exercise. Why is the widened eight-bit approximation exactly copied even though it is still an inaccurate representation of decimal 0.1?

Answer. The copy’s exact input is the stored eight-bit binary value. That dyadic value fits into 128 bits without rounding. Its discrepancy from the original decimal real number arose during the earlier parse, and the copy has no access to that lost information.

6 Arithmetic, rounding, and exponent ranges

A reliable calculation starts with three separate choices: what numbers the inputs represent, how many bits each destination will retain, and which rounding rule each operation will use. The context also determines the permitted exponent range. These choices answer different questions. More precision places representable values closer together; a wider exponent range allows larger and smaller magnitudes. Neither change can recover information already discarded when an input was created.

This chapter develops the numerical meaning of an arithmetic call and shows how to read its result. The complete example is numeric_ranges.c. It uses deliberately small precision so that the rounding decisions can be checked by hand.

6.1 The destination determines the precision

For a regular value with precision pp, Polyphase Float stores an integer significand MM, a sign ss, and a normalized exponent ee. Its value is

x=sM2e−p,2p−1≤M<2p. x=sM2^{e-p},\qquad 2^{p-1}\le M<2^p.

Thus a regular magnitude lies in [2e−1,2e)[2^{e-1},2^e). Within this interval the spacing is 2e−p2^{e-p}. Precision counts significant binary bits, including the leading bit. It does not count decimal places after a decimal point.

In a call such as

int t = ppf_div(&quotient, &numerator, &denominator,
                PPF_RNDN, &ctx);

quotient supplies the result precision. The inputs may have different precisions. Their stored values are the operands of the division; the library does not reinterpret them as unknown higher-precision originals. Increasing the context’s default precision affects subsequent initialization using that default. It does not change the precision of objects that already exist.

For planning output, plog102p\log_{10}2 is a useful approximate count of significant decimal digits. For example, 128 bits correspond to about 38.5 decimal digits. This estimate is not an error bound for a long computation. Cancellation, input uncertainty, conditioning, and intermediate rounding still matter.

6.2 Choose the rounding rule deliberately

The five deterministic rounding modes have straightforward geometric meanings. Consider rounding the positive exact value 1/31/3 to three binary bits. The neighboring values are 5/16=0.31255/16=0.3125 and 3/8=0.3753/8=0.375.

Mode Rule Three-bit result for 1/31/3
PPF_RNDN Nearest; a midpoint selects the even significand 0.3125
PPF_RNDZ Toward zero 0.3125
PPF_RNDU Toward positive infinity 0.375
PPF_RNDD Toward negative infinity 0.3125
PPF_RNDA Away from zero 0.375

For negative values, upward still means toward positive infinity. It therefore moves a negative inexact result toward zero. Downward moves it away from zero. Thinking in terms of the number line avoids a common sign error when constructing bounds.

PPF_RND_DEFAULT requests the context’s configured mode. Explicit modes are usually easier to review in numerical algorithms, especially when adjacent calls intentionally form lower and upper bounds.

PPF_RNDF requests faithful rounding. Code that needs a specified direction, an exactness decision from the return value, or reproducible choice between neighboring values should use a deterministic mode. Do not build a certificate from an assumed faithful ternary convention. The examples in this manual use explicit deterministic modes whenever they inspect the ternary result.

6.3 Read the ternary value before interpreting flags

Most arithmetic functions return a ternary direction. With a deterministic rounding mode and a successful ordinary numerical result, zero means exact, positive means the stored result is greater than the exact mathematical result of that call, and negative means it is smaller. The magnitude of the integer is not an error estimate. A return value of 1 does not mean one bit or one unit in the last place was lost.

Check the failure sentinel first:

int t = ppf_mul(&product, &a, &b, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
if (t == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) {
    /* Diagnose the failure; product is not a usable new answer. */
} else if (t == 0) {
    /* For an ordinary finite result, the multiplication is exact. */
} else {
    /* A valid rounded result; the sign of t gives its direction. */
}

Testing if (t) as an error condition rejects ordinary inexact arithmetic. Conversely, testing only t < 0 confuses an error sentinel with a legitimate downward rounding direction. Special values also require their documented classification rules: a numerical NaN can be the specified result of a domain error rather than a failure to execute the API.

Not every integer-returning function uses this convention. Reuse an error-handling pattern only for functions with the same return contract.

Interface Return interpretation
Initialization functions and ppf_set_str Status code; successful parsing is not a claim of exact numerical representation
ppf_get_constant_interval Status: 0 for success, -1 for failure
ppf_div_with_plan_many Batch status: 0 for success, -1 for failure; individual rounding directions are written to the optional ternaries array
ppf_set_dyadic_interval DECIDED, UNDECIDED, or ERROR; its ternary is a separate output
ppf_modf, ppf_sin_cos, ppf_sinh_cosh Packed two-output code on success, not one scalar ternary

For a successful paired call in a deterministic mode, each output contributes a field: 0 means exact, 1 means rounded above its exact component, and 2 means rounded below it. The combined code is the first output’s field plus four times the second output’s field. The output order is integer/fractional for ppf_modf, sine/cosine for ppf_sin_cos, and hyperbolic sine/cosine for ppf_sinh_cosh. Check PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before decoding. A positive combined code can therefore include a downward-rounded component; its sign is not a rounding direction. Special-value cases still require numerical classification.

6.4 Precision and range are independent

The context restricts regular exponents to emin <= e <= emax. The smallest positive regular value is

2emin−1, 2^{\mathrm{emin}-1},

and, at precision pp, the largest positive finite value is

(1−2−p)2emax. (1-2^{-p})2^{\mathrm{emax}}.

These formulas use the normalized exponent convention above. Treating emin as the exponent of the smallest power of two would introduce a factor-of-two mistake.

The default exponent range is intentionally much wider than a native double range. The absolute bounds accepted by the context API are exposed through the public constants and range-query functions. Wide representational limits do not imply that every algorithm can economically process every combination of precision and exponent. Some operations impose checked workspace or iteration limits.

Changing a context’s range does not rewrite every object previously created with that context. Set the intended range before the calculation where possible. If applying a restricted range to a result calculated in a wider context, use ppf_check_range with the correct incoming ternary from that calculation. Inventing an incoming zero discards information needed to avoid a second-rounding error at a boundary.

6.5 A range example you can verify by hand

The example initializes two eight-bit inputs and a two-bit destination, then sets the context range to [-9,9]. It computes

7152−10=716815≈477.8667. \frac{7}{15\,2^{-10}}=\frac{7168}{15}\approx477.8667.

The largest finite destination value is 3⋅27=3843\cdot2^7=384. The next value in an unbounded exponent system is 512. Their midpoint is 448, so nearest rounding chooses 512 before the exponent restriction is applied. Since that exponent is outside the context range, the final result is positive infinity with overflow and inexact flags.

Toward-zero rounding selects 384 directly. That rounded value fits the exponent range, so this call raises inexact without overflow. This example illustrates why comparing the exact magnitude with the largest finite value is insufficient to predict every range flag: the rounding mode matters.

The program prints:

Nearest quotient: +infinity; overflow and inexact.
Toward-zero quotient: 384; inexact only.
Exact subnormal emulation: underflow without inexact.

The final line comes from a separate subnormal-emulation calculation described below. Every line is printed only after the program checks the value, return direction, and relevant flags. A failed check produces a nonzero process exit.

6.6 Flags describe events, and they accumulate

Context flags are sticky. An inexact flag can remain set after a later exact operation. Save or clear flags at a meaningful boundary, perform the operation or group of operations, and then inspect the resulting mask. In an explicit-context program, use the ppf_context_flags_* functions with that same context. The short forms operate on the calling thread’s default context.

Flag Practical interpretation
PPF_FLAG_INEXACT A rounded operation recorded loss of exact representability
PPF_FLAG_UNDERFLOW The operation encountered its underflow condition; subnormal emulation has a specific rule
PPF_FLAG_OVERFLOW The rounded exponent exceeded the permitted range
PPF_FLAG_DIVBY0 A documented pole or division-by-zero case occurred
PPF_FLAG_NAN An invalid numerical input or domain case produced NaN
PPF_FLAG_ERANGE A request could not be completed under the applicable representation, domain, or certification limits
PPF_FLAG_ALLOC A request to the configured Polyphase allocator failed

An inexact result is normal for division by three or evaluation of an irrational constant. It is usually not an application error. Allocation failure, a domain error, and an exhausted certification path require different responses even if more than one flag is present. Record the requested operation and its input policy alongside the flags; the mask alone is not a complete diagnostic message.

6.7 Emulating subnormal arithmetic

A ppf_t has regular values and signed zero, but no separate stored subnormal category. ppf_subnormalize emulates a fixed-point region by reducing effective precision according to the current exponent and emin. In that region the spacing becomes the fixed quantum 2emin−12^{\mathrm{emin}-1}.

The function needs the rounding mode and ternary from the operation that produced its input. It uses that information when a second rounding would otherwise choose the wrong side of a midpoint. Its returned ternary describes the final value relative to the original exact result, not merely relative to the intermediate input.

When the subnormal step actually reduces effective precision, it raises underflow even when the value remains exact. This follows the mpfr_subnormalize-style API rule. In the example, precision is two, emin is -30, and the input is exactly 2−312^{-31}. The value remains unchanged and the ternary is zero, yet underflow is set. Inexact remains clear. Do not apply the ordinary “underflow must imply inexact” shortcut to this API.

6.8 Select arithmetic that matches the expression

Use a fused operation when the mathematical specification calls for one rounding of a combined expression. ppf_fma evaluates ab+cab+c with a single final rounding; separate multiplication and addition round an intermediate product. Near cancellation, these are different numerical computations. The same design consideration applies to fused two-product operations, sums, dot products, and ppf_hypot.

For roots, select the operation that expresses the intended degree and sign convention. Odd roots of negative real values are meaningful; even roots of negative real values are not real. Negative degrees introduce reciprocals and their zero-domain conditions. The reference distinguishes ppf_rootn_ui, ppf_rootn_si, and the older ppf_root interface, including their signed-zero conventions.

Aliasing is a separate contract. Many scalar operations support replacing an input with their output, but this does not authorize arbitrary overlap in paired or batched operations. Use the documented alias pattern, especially when outputs may be written concurrently. Numerical correctness, supported memory overlap, and successful allocation are three requirements that must all hold for a reliable call.

7 Constants and certified intervals

A long string of digits is useful for display, but it is a weak foundation for a numerical constant. The last supplied digit may be rounded in the wrong direction for the caller’s purpose, and the string may not contain enough information to answer a higher-precision request. Polyphase Float’s constant interface is built around enclosures: lower and upper bounds known to contain the mathematical constant.

This chapter explains how to request a constant, how to export its enclosure, and what an interval decision actually certifies. The complete example is numeric_constants.c. The independent square-root refinement example in Numerical recipes shows how an application can supply its own justified enclosure.

7.1 Request the constant you mean

The public constant family includes four values:

Function Mathematical value
ppf_const_pi π\pi, the circle constant
ppf_const_log2 log2\log 2, the natural logarithm of two
ppf_const_euler Euler–Mascheroni constant γ\gamma
ppf_const_catalan Catalan’s constant GG

Euler’s constant is not the exponential base ee, and log2 in the constant name denotes the value log2\log 2. By contrast, the function ppf_log2(x) evaluates the base-two logarithm of its argument. Keeping these names distinct avoids a subtle substitution error in formulas.

Initialize the destination at the desired precision and call the selected function with an explicit rounding mode and context. In a deterministic mode, a successful ternary has the same direction meaning as for arithmetic. The destination precision, not the length of a later printed decimal string, determines the computed binary result.

For an upper bound on π\pi, request PPF_RNDU; for a lower bound, request PPF_RNDD. A nearest-rounded approximation does not automatically provide either side. If an application subsequently multiplies a lower bound by a negative number, the inequality direction reverses. Bounds remain meaningful only when every subsequent operation respects signs and monotonicity.

7.2 What a dyadic enclosure contains

The interval-export interface returns GMP integers L,UL,U and a binary exponent ee, with

L2e≤c≤U2e. L2^e\le c\le U2^e.

Both endpoint values are exact because the integer and power-of-two representation is exact. The width is (U−L)2e(U-L)2^e. It is an absolute width, not a relative-error estimate and not a count of correct decimal digits.

A negative exponent does not mean the constant itself is small. For example, a large integer multiplied by 2−S2^{-S} can represent a number near three. The common scale simply permits both endpoints to be recorded without first rounding them to an ordinary floating-point object.

ppf_get_constant_interval accepts a constant identifier, initialized GMP output integers, an exponent output pointer, requested precision, and worker count. It returns status: 0 for success and -1 for failure, rather than a ternary. It has no explicit context argument: its work is governed through the thread-default path. This distinction matters in applications that otherwise use a custom explicit context. Do not assume an unrelated context’s allocator or flags govern this export call.

The destination precision used later for rounding the enclosure is independent of the precision requested for interval construction. A practical pattern is to request a somewhat tighter interval, try the desired destination rounding, and refine only if needed. The number of extra bits is a work policy, not a proof by itself.

7.3 The decision requires more than matching endpoints

The public interval assignment call is

ppf_interval_status_t s = ppf_set_dyadic_interval(
    &result, lower, upper, exponent, rounding, &ternary, &ctx);

Its three outcomes have different meanings:

Status Meaning Normal caller response
PPF_INTERVAL_DECIDED The enclosure determines the destination value, ternary direction, and compatible range flags Use the result and recorded certificate
PPF_INTERVAL_UNDECIDED The available enclosure does not establish the full requested decision Obtain tighter justified bounds and retry
PPF_INTERVAL_ERROR The request failed its validation or execution requirements Diagnose the context and arguments

A decided result requires the two rounded endpoints to select the same value. It also requires a proven ternary relation and agreeing underflow and overflow decisions. Endpoint agreement alone is insufficient.

To understand the ternary requirement, suppose both endpoints round to a representable number rr, but the interval straddles rr. Some possible exact values are below rr, others above it. The final floating-point value is determined, but its direction relative to the unknown exact value is not. A non-singleton interval containing rr does not establish that the answer is exactly rr, either. The correct outcome is undecided.

Likewise, an interval can cross a range-flag boundary while both endpoints happen to select the same stored value. A full decision must resolve that ambiguity. This is why an application’s stopping rule should use the returned interval status instead of comparing two printed numbers.

7.4 Undecided is useful information

An undecided result preserves the destination, the caller’s ternary output variable, and the existing context flags. This makes refinement convenient: a previous valid result remains available while a new enclosure is being improved. It does not mean the previous value solves the new problem.

Keep a separate Boolean or application status indicating whether the current request has been certified. A destination containing an old value is still a valid object, but validity of storage is not validity of the new numerical answer. The refinement example starts the destination at one and uses a recognizable ternary marker so that this distinction is explicit.

An error has a different contract. Do not extend the undecided preservation guarantee to every error code or every arithmetic API. In particular, a numerical failure can leave a numerical error result, while a governed project-allocation failure has its own rollback rule. These cases are discussed further in Special functions.

7.5 Walking through the constant example

numeric_constants.c creates two 80-bit destinations. It evaluates π\pi directly into the first, exports a 160-bit enclosure, and asks the interval interface to round that enclosure into the second. It checks both value equality and equality of ternary signs.

The expected output is:

Pi: direct evaluation and exported interval agree at 80 bits.
The interval proves the value and its rounding direction.

The program deliberately does not test a particular decimal spelling or a cache-hit count. Those observations are not the property being demonstrated. Its useful invariant is that the direct API and the exported enclosure establish the same 80-bit answer and direction.

This agreement is a consistency check within the constant subsystem.
