Other interfaces use other conventions. ppf_set_str returns zero on successful complete conversion, while ppf_strtofr returns a ternary relation or its error sentinel and also reports an end pointer. PPFIF import/export use zero for success. Formatting returns a byte count or a negative failure result. Stream text functions return counts. A generic wrapper must preserve these distinctions instead of converting every nonzero integer to an error.

Flags are sticky and describe the context on which they were raised. Clear the relevant flags before an isolated diagnostic call, read them immediately afterward, and preserve them before unrelated output formatting can change another context. A normal return together with PPF_FLAG_ALLOC can describe a successful fallback after a preferred allocation was refused.

15.2 Numerical symptoms

Symptom What to examine Practical next step
A correct-looking result is reported as an error Was a nonzero ternary result treated as failure? Compare with PPF_TERNARY_ERROR; report inexactness separately
A value unexpectedly becomes NaN after changing precision Was ppf_set_prec used? Use ppf_prec_round when the old value must be retained and rounded
Increasing an input’s precision does not improve the result What is the destination precision, and how were the inputs originally obtained? Increase working and destination precision deliberately; reconstruct inputs from exact source data
Decimal input differs from its decimal spelling Is the value exactly representable in binary at this precision? Inspect inexactness and rounding; use an exact integer/rational source when appropriate
Printing fewer digits seems to change the result Is the discrepancy only in the formatted representation? Compare stored values independently of their display strings
A result overflows or becomes tiny unexpectedly Is the intended context range active? Record emin, emax, and the explicit/default context choice before the call
Flags appear unrelated to the current operation Were earlier sticky flags retained, or was the wrong context queried? Clear and inspect the same context around the operation
A special function returns an error on finite input Is the input admitted, and could the bounded evaluator resolve it? Check the function’s domain and construction limits; retain the flags and exact input for diagnosis
Faithful results differ in the last bit Is the comparison expecting a unique nearest result? Check the faithful-rounding contract or choose a specified directed/nearest mode

More precision cannot repair information lost before the value entered the library. Passing a decimal literal through a C double first fixes it to that binary approximation. Reading the original string or constructing the exact rational gives the high-precision calculation the intended starting data. Similarly, a later high-precision destination cannot undo an earlier rounded intermediate. Identify the first irreversible rounding step before adding precision everywhere.

For a suspected numerical defect, reduce the calculation while retaining the same rounding mode, precision, range, and special-value categories. Compare out-of-place and permitted in-place forms when aliasing is involved. If an independent reference is used, match precision and exponent policy on both sides and distinguish a reference disagreement from a proven library defect. Keep the original failing input even if a smaller reproducer is found.

15.3 Text, files, and ownership symptoms

Symptom Likely check Practical next step
A parsed field accepts an unwanted suffix Was the prefix parser used without checking endptr? Use ppf_set_str, or validate the suffix explicitly
Text output cannot be read back Base, exponent marker, locale, or too few digits may differ Define the text grammar and locale; use PPFIF for saved objects
ppf_get_str digits look too large by a power of the base The separate exponent may have been ignored Place the radix point before the first digit and apply the returned exponent
A formatted buffer is silently incomplete Was the snprintf required length checked? Treat a nonnegative length at least as large as capacity as truncation
Freeing a returned string crashes Which interface allocated it? Pair ppf_get_str with ppf_free_str, and ppf_asprintf with free
An imported object’s precision changes PPFIF restores encoded precision Import into a temporary, then assign into the desired working precision
A small binary record is rejected for resources The encoded precision can require large significand storage Check the 64 MiB default import bounds and the producer’s record metadata
Retrying failed input starts at the wrong place Input consumption is not rolled back with the number Reposition a seekable stream or restore an application-owned input buffer

Do not diagnose a saved record solely from its extension. PPFIF has its own identifier, layout, and integrity check. MPFR FPIF, a raw structure dump, and a text number are different representations. A checksum mismatch is a reason to reject a record; removing the check to make an import succeed conceals the problem. Retain a bounded failing record and the producer’s identity when investigating interoperability.

15.4 Allocation and concurrency symptoms

Symptom What to examine Practical next step
Clearing one number damages another Were live structures copied by assignment or memcpy? Use initialized destinations with ppf_set, or exchange ownership with ppf_swap
A custom allocator fails during cleanup Did its opaque state or pool expire too early? Keep allocator state alive until all dependent objects, strings, and contexts are cleared
A failed resize destroys the original block Does the custom reallocator preserve its input on failure? Correct the callback contract before retrying numerical work
Memory remains after a large calculation Is it an arena, thread workspace, or global cache? Clean the relevant owner at a deliberate lifecycle boundary
Several threads occasionally produce corrupted state Are a context, destination, random state, or raw buffer shared mutably? Give workers private state or protect the whole affected operation with a lock
More workers make a workload slower Are internal teams competing with application workers? Measure one parallel layer first, then compare controlled configurations
Shutdown or library unload crashes Can another thread still call the library or run its destructor? Join workers and release their state before unloading

An allocation flag does not identify every process allocation. If a GMP or system allocation fails outside the recoverable project allocator domain, the ordinary destination-preservation guarantee is not a complete recovery strategy. Likewise, a custom allocator that returns an invalid pointer or reports a false capacity breaks the caller contract. Start fault-injection tests with a simple, correctly accounting allocator and a valid initialized destination, as in the allocation example.

15.5 Build and deployment symptoms

Symptom Practical next step
GMP header or library discovery fails Install matching development files and check compiler architecture and search paths
A core-only consumer unexpectedly requests MPFR Use find_package with COMPONENTS core
The adapter is unavailable after installation Build it with official MPFR development headers and request COMPONENTS mpfr in the consumer
A static link has unresolved dependencies Use the exported static target or pkg-config’s static dependency flags; remember that selecting an archive is a separate step
A program links but cannot load a shared library Correct its installed runtime-library search configuration
OpenMP configuration or linking fails Select the matching compiler runtime, or build with PPF_OPENMP=OFF
An executable fails with an illegal instruction elsewhere Check native compiler tuning and the target CPU instruction set
Tests or examples are absent from a build Review CMake feature detection and build options, then list configured tests

When a build behaves inconsistently after a compiler or sanitizer change, configure a new directory before investigating numerical code. Run one small installed consumer to distinguish package discovery and loader problems from failures inside a larger application. Capture the actual library path and runtime version, not only the version requested in a build script.

15.6 Prepare a useful diagnostic record

A concise reproducer should initialize its own objects and contexts, contain the exact input construction, perform the failing operation, check the result, and clean up. Include the precision of every relevant object, the rounding mode, exponent limits, return value, and flag mask. For a parser problem, include the bytes or a safely bounded file, the base, and the first unconsumed position. For an aliasing problem, state which pointers refer to the same object. For a concurrency problem, identify which resources are shared and the point at which readers finish.

Also record compiler and dependency versions, build options, optional interfaces, worker settings, and whether the failure occurs in a fresh process. Keep the original diagnostic output and distinguish an actual failure from a test that was never executed. A missing executable permission, an unavailable sanitizer runtime, or a timeout is useful evidence, but none is a passing numerical result. These details make a report actionable without requiring another reader to reconstruct the application’s entire environment.

16 Numerical limits and admission policies

Arbitrary precision makes the precision a parameter. It does not remove finite storage, bounded certification, or the need to validate an argument before constructing a large intermediate. This chapter explains how to treat those limits in an application. The source-level inventory in docs/NUMERICAL_LIMITS.md records the individual policies and the available boundary evidence.

16.1 Range, domain, and work are different constraints

A mathematical domain restriction concerns whether a real-valued answer exists under the operation’s definition. A configured exponent range concerns which answers can be represented in the current context. A work limit bounds a particular implementation route. These restrictions can produce different status values, flags, and destinations. Do not infer one from another.

A shortcut can decline an input while a general evaluator remains available. An evaluator can also exhaust its finite certification budget and return a numerical error. Raising the destination precision may make a later attempt more expensive without settling the original uncertainty. Check the actual result rather than treating a larger precision as a universal remedy.

Path Current policy Application consequence
Parsed textual exponents Direct power construction has an absolute exponent budget of 2,000,000. Larger cases require a justified range classification or may be rejected. Validate input sizes and check parse status.
Ordinary periodic trigonometric reduction The general path can reject a request needing more than 1,000,000 extra reduction bits. Prefer exact scaled-grid interfaces when the input is naturally specified in that form.
Finite Airy Ai input The admitted absolute input is at most 500, compared exactly. Check the domain before requesting work outside it.
General integer-order Bessel paths Finite order magnitude is bounded by 100,000. Do not interpret rejection as a proof that the mathematical function is undefined.
PPFIF import The default maximum is 64 MiB for both payload and limb-rounded significand storage. Keep the default for untrusted data unless the application deliberately chooses another positive cap.
General dyadic certificate construction Endpoint alignment is limited to 1,000,000 extra bits by default. An unusable enclosure can cause refinement or numerical rejection.
Exponential-minus-one construction The same extra-bit cap bounds an intermediate endpoint’s exponent gap from one before subtraction. A compact enormous input need not be expanded into an enormous exact intermediate.
Negative-parameter incomplete Gamma at finite positive second argument Recurrence admission requires the first argument to be at least -100,000. Separate special-value paths have their own rules. Test the admission condition before relying on this recurrence path.
Negative-integer zeta Large negative even integers are recognized directly as exact zeros. The small odd-integer Bernoulli shortcut is admitted before integer expansion. A shortcut threshold is not a claim that all other zeta arguments are outside the mathematical domain.

The default import limit can be changed through the documented PPF_FPIF_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES build configuration. The dyadic extra-bit budget is an alignment policy, not a global ceiling on destination precision. A series term count is likewise not the same quantity as an input exponent or a byte allocation limit.

16.2 Attempts and fallback routes

The implementation uses distinct budgets for distinct algorithms. General transcendental and special-function certification, root refinement, interval arithmetic, constant builders, text conversion, and fast shortcuts do not all share a single retry count. Individual series and recurrences have their own iteration and admission checks. The source inventory identifies these separately instead of presenting one number as a library-wide limit.

Many of those numbers control efficiency or a particular route. A fast path may decline and fall back. A builder can stop without a certificate. A final evaluator may reject after bounded attempts. Only a proven enclosure and a successful settlement justify a certified returned result. Counting attempts, or observing that a last term is small, does not supply that proof.

The numerical-arguments reference in docs/NUMERICAL_ARGUMENTS.md connects reviewed paths to their enclosure or remainder arguments and records remaining obligations. Its distinction between a written argument and finite execution evidence matters: both are useful, and neither should be silently substituted for the other.

16.3 Handling a numerical rejection

For an operation whose contract uses the numerical ternary convention:

  1. Check for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before reading its sign.
  2. Inspect the operation’s flags and documented output state.
  3. If the operation committed NaN on certification or admission failure, do not keep using the old destination as if it were still present.
  4. Decide whether to choose another supported representation, change a justified precision or range parameter, report the unsupported request, or use another algorithm with its own checked contract.

This sequence does not turn every error into the same case. Invalid arguments, an unsupported resource request, and a recoverable project-allocation failure can follow different paths. Transactional allocation rollback preserves the prior numerical destination on an unrecovered project-allocation failure, but sticky flags may change. GMP allocations, I/O side effects, and application callbacks remain outside that rollback guarantee.

16.4 Designing application limits

Give the application its own input, precision, time, and output-size budgets. These should reflect its purpose and the resources actually available. Check string lengths and exponent syntax before accepting a large batch. Cap import bytes and total record counts. Estimate the total working set before assigning one large object to every worker. Treat output formatting as work too: a small stored value can still be asked to produce a very large number of digits.

When retaining a failure report, record the function, exact input encoding, destination precision, rounding mode, context range, flags, and return value. Keep the source version and build features with that record. An exact binary or hexadecimal input is more useful than a shortened decimal display when reproducing a rounding boundary.

16.5 Interpreting validation

The example suite checks its complete programs and expected outputs. Numerical regressions exercise selected domains and resource boundaries. Sanitizers inspect the executions they observe. Differential comparisons test agreement on their enumerated cases. These results support concrete engineering claims. They do not imply support for an untested platform, unbounded precision, or every admitted input.

A stable public contract can state its finite limits plainly. It should also state which mathematical and execution obligations remain open. The release readiness record carries those obligations separately from this user’s guide.

17 Core API reference

This reference covers every core function declared in <polyphase_float.h>. The five optional MPFR adapter functions are described separately in the integration chapter. Entries are arranged by task, then by name. Use PDF search or the alphabetical index to find a symbol.

All ordinary arithmetic objects must be initialized and valid. Unless an operation explicitly changes precision, the destination’s precision governs its result. Mutating an object or an explicit context requires exclusive access. No function transfers ownership unless its entry says so.

A recorded allocation contract describes recoverable project allocation, not every allocation made by GMP, libc, or the operating system. Numerical range rejection and certification exhaustion have their own output rules. In particular, an error sentinel alone is not a promise of destination preservation.

The numerical-limits appendix applies throughout this reference. Absence of a function-specific limit in an entry is not a claim of unlimited work, a termination proof, or universal correct rounding. The full source and individual numerical arguments remain the authority for implementation details.

17.1 Contexts, allocators, flags, and scratch memory

17.1.1 ppf_allocflag_p

Report whether the allocation-failure flag is set in the calling thread default context.

int ppf_allocflag_p(void);

Result. A predicate result: zero means false and a nonzero value means true.

Concurrency. This operation concerns the calling thread’s state; it is not a mechanism for sharing a mutable context.

17.1.2 ppf_arena_alloc

Allocate temporary aligned memory from a context scratch arena.

void *ppf_arena_alloc(ppf_context_t *ctx, size_t bytes, size_t alignment);

Result. A pointer with the ownership conditions below. Failure indicator: NULL where documented.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

Ownership. storage remains owned by the context until release, reset, or clear.

Allocation and failure. On unrecovered project-allocation failure, returns NULL without adding a new arena block or changing the existing arena allocation position; earlier arena allocations remain valid.

17.1.3 ppf_arena_mark

Mark the current scratch-arena position.

ppf_arena_mark_t ppf_arena_mark(const ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. The value described above, with the declared C return type.

17.1.4 ppf_arena_release

Release scratch allocations made after a saved arena mark.

void ppf_arena_release(ppf_context_t *ctx, ppf_arena_mark_t mark);

Result. No return value.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.1.5 ppf_arena_reset

Reset the context scratch arena for reuse.

void ppf_arena_reset(ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. No return value.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.1.6 ppf_clear_allocflag

Clear the allocation-failure flag in the calling thread default context.

void ppf_clear_allocflag(void);

Result. No return value.

Concurrency. This operation concerns the calling thread’s state; it is not a mechanism for sharing a mutable context.

17.1.7 ppf_context_clear

Release memory owned by an explicit context.

void ppf_context_clear(ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. No return value.

Context and rounding. The supplied context must be non-null and initialized.

17.1.8 ppf_context_clone

Create a new context with the same policy settings as another context.

int ppf_context_clone(ppf_context_t *dst, const ppf_context_t *src);

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Context and rounding. The supplied context must be non-null and initialized.

17.1.9 ppf_context_flags

Read all exception flags from a context.

ppf_flags_t ppf_context_flags(const ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. The value described above, with the declared C return type.

17.1.10 ppf_context_flags_clear

Clear selected exception flags in a context.

void ppf_context_flags_clear(ppf_context_t *ctx, ppf_flags_t mask);

Result. No return value.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.1.11 ppf_context_flags_restore

Restore selected context flags from a saved value.

void ppf_context_flags_restore(
    ppf_context_t *ctx,
    ppf_flags_t flags,
    ppf_flags_t mask
);

Result. No return value.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.1.12 ppf_context_flags_save

Copy the current context flags for later restoration.

ppf_flags_t ppf_context_flags_save(const ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. The value described above, with the declared C return type.

17.1.13 ppf_context_flags_set

Set selected exception flags in a context.

void ppf_context_flags_set(ppf_context_t *ctx, ppf_flags_t mask);

Result. No return value.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.1.14 ppf_context_init

Initialize an explicit context with default precision, range, rounding, flags, allocator, and scratch arena.

int ppf_context_init(ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Context and rounding. The context destination must be non-null writable unused storage. This call initializes it; do not overwrite a live context.

17.1.15 ppf_context_init_custom

Initialize a context that uses caller-supplied allocation callbacks.

int ppf_context_init_custom(
    ppf_context_t *ctx,
    const ppf_allocator_t *allocator
);

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Context and rounding. The context destination must be non-null writable unused storage. This call initializes it; do not overwrite a live context.

17.1.16 ppf_context_set_default_precision

Change the precision used for new default-precision objects in a context.

int ppf_context_set_default_precision(
    ppf_context_t *ctx,

    ppf_rnd_t rnd,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Result. A numerical ternary result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before interpreting its sign.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

Overlap. the floating destination may alias each floating source position exercised by the aliasing matrix.

Allocation and failure. Reviewed valid initialized-storage paths do not call the project allocator; existing capacity, direct-storage and ownership preconditions apply; GMP allocation is outside this claim.

17.5.15 ppf_sgn

Return the mathematical sign of a non-NaN value and update context state when needed.

int ppf_sgn(const ppf_t *x, ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. A sign result for the operation described above.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.5.16 ppf_signbit

Return the stored sign bit, including for zero, infinity, and NaN.

int ppf_signbit(const ppf_t *x);

Result. A predicate result: zero means false and a nonzero value means true.

17.5.17 ppf_zero_p

Test whether a value is zero.

int ppf_zero_p(const ppf_t *x);

Result. A predicate result: zero means false and a nonzero value means true.

17.7 Initialize-and-set shortcuts

17.7.1 ppf_init_set

Initialize a number and copy-round another Polyphase number into it.

int ppf_init_set(
    ppf_t *rop,
    const ppf_t *op,
    ppf_rnd_t rnd,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Result. A numerical ternary result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before interpreting its sign.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

Overlap. destination is uninitialized and distinct from the initialized source; Forbidden: destination and source are the same object.

Allocation and failure. Every observed project-allocation failure is tested; initialization failure leaves a safe-zero object, setter failure leaves an initialized clearable object; caller must clear after any initialized outcome.

    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Result. A numerical ternary result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before interpreting its sign.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

Overlap. destination storage satisfies the function’s initialization or destruction precondition; Forbidden: using an already initialized object as an initialization destination unless explicitly documented.

Allocation and failure. Every observed project-allocation failure is tested; initialization failure leaves a safe-zero object, setter failure leaves an initialized clearable object; caller must clear after any initialized outcome.

Ownership. on success *text is allocated with the process allocator and must be released with free.

Allocation and failure. Sets text to NULL before formatting; failure releases temporary storage and leaves text NULL, rather than preserving its prior pointer; %n writes already performed while formatting are not rolled back.

17.9.10 ppf_fpif_export

Write the endian-independent PPFIF01 binary interchange representation.

int ppf_fpif_export(FILE *stream, const ppf_t *op);

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Allocation and failure. The complete record is staged before its first stream write; project-allocation failure leaves the stream and source number unchanged, but a later stream write failure may leave a partial record.

17.9.11 ppf_fpif_import

Transactionally import a PPFIF01 record; malformed input leaves the destination unchanged.

int ppf_fpif_import(ppf_t *op, FILE *stream, ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

Allocation and failure. Unrecovered project-allocation failure preserves the numerical destination and releases temporary project-owned storage; bytes already consumed from the input stream are not restored.

Resource policy. default 64 MiB cap independently bounds imported payload and rounded significand storage (536870912 ordinary precision bits on GMP64); PPF_FPIF_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES may configure another positive cap; initial staging is at most 4096 bytes, growing only after reserved bytes arrive; range rejection returns -1, raises ERANGE and preserves the destination. Consult the numerical-limits appendix for the complete cap inventory.

Result. A formatting count; a negative result reports failure.

Allocation and failure. Formatting completes in temporary storage before stream output; unrecovered project-allocation failure during formatting leaves the stream unchanged; %n writes already performed are not rolled back, and a later stream write failure may leave partial output.

Result. A borrowed pointer. Do not free the returned storage. Failure indicator: NULL where documented.

Ownership. returned string is library-owned static storage.

17.14.2 ppf_abi_epoch

Return the governed public ABI epoch.

uint32_t ppf_abi_epoch(void);

Result. The value described above, with the declared C return type.

17.14.3 ppf_abi_info_size

Return the size of the current ABI information structure.

size_t ppf_abi_info_size(void);

Result. The operation-specific count described above, rather than a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: 0 when the operation cannot produce a count.

17.14.4 ppf_abi_revision

Return the additive revision within the current ABI epoch.

uint32_t ppf_abi_revision(void);

Result. The value described above, with the declared C return type.

17.14.5 ppf_abi_tag

Return the stable textual tag for the current ABI epoch.

const char *ppf_abi_tag(void);

Result. A borrowed pointer. Do not free the returned storage. Failure indicator: NULL where documented.

Ownership. returned string is library-owned static storage.

17.14.6 ppf_buildopt_thread_cleanup_p

Report whether automatic POSIX thread-exit cleanup is available in this build.

int ppf_buildopt_thread_cleanup_p(void);

Result. A predicate result: zero means false and a nonzero value means true.

17.14.7 ppf_get_abi_info

Copy a size-bounded runtime description of the active public ABI into caller storage.

int ppf_get_abi_info(ppf_abi_info_t *info, size_t info_size);

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

17.15 Arithmetic and product planning

17.15.1 ppf_add

Add two Polyphase values with one final rounding.

int ppf_add(
    ppf_t *rop,
    const ppf_t *a,
    const ppf_t *b,
    ppf_rnd_t rnd,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Result. A numerical ternary result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before interpreting its sign.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

Overlap. the floating destination may alias each floating source position exercised by the aliasing matrix.

Allocation and failure. An unrecovered project-allocation failure preserves the prior numerical output. Sticky flags may change, and an exact fallback may succeed while retaining the allocation flag. Numerical rejection is a separate case and may commit NaN.

17.16 Roots and hypotenuse

17.16.1 ppf_cbrt

Compute the real cube root.

Input contract. defined for finite real inputs.

Result. A numerical ternary result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before interpreting its sign.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

Overlap. the floating destination may alias each floating source position exercised by the aliasing matrix.

Allocation and failure. An unrecovered project-allocation failure preserves the prior numerical output. Sticky flags may change, and an exact fallback may succeed while retaining the allocation flag. Numerical rejection is a separate case and may commit NaN.

Resource policy. nontrivial exact-input root interval construction uses PPF_ROOT_ATTEMPTS refinement attempts (default 10); exact and exceptional-value cases may return earlier. Consult the numerical-limits appendix for the complete cap inventory.

Input contract. plan and every output/numerator entry must be valid.

Overlap. outputsi may equal numeratorsi for each index; Forbidden: duplicate outputs and cross-index output/input overlap.

17.17.6 ppf_divisor_plan_create

Create an immutable plan for repeatedly dividing into one destination precision.

int ppf_divisor_plan_create(
    ppf_divisor_plan_t **out,
    const ppf_t *denominator,
    ppf_prec_t destination_precision,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Input contract. denominator must be finite and nonzero; destination precision must be valid.

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

Ownership. successful creation returns a plan released by ppf_divisor_plan_destroy.

Concurrency. Application locking is required for shared mutable use.

Create a reusable divisor plan with an expected application count for planning.

    ppf_divisor_plan_t **out,

    ppf_prec_t destination_precision,
    unsigned long expected_applications,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Input contract. denominator must be finite and nonzero; destination precision must be valid.

Result. A status code. Check the operation’s success convention; this is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: function-specific nonzero failure status.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

Ownership. successful creation returns a plan released by ppf_divisor_plan_destroy.

Allocation and failure. After initial argument validation, out is set to NULL; project-allocation failure releases the incomplete plan and leaves out NULL and the denominator unchanged; this does not preserve an existing pointer passed through out.

Concurrency. Application locking is required for shared mutable use.

Concurrency. Application locking is required for shared mutable use.

17.19.29 ppf_sin_cos

Compute sine and cosine into two outputs.

int ppf_sin_cos(
    ppf_t *sop,
    ppf_t *cop,
    const ppf_t *op,
    ppf_rnd_t rnd,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before decoding. Otherwise the return is code(first) + 4 * code(second), where 0 means exact, 1 means above the exact result, and 2 means below it: the sine output first and the cosine output second. The sign of the packed return is not a numerical ternary. Failure indicator: PPF_TERNARY_ERROR.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

17.19.31 ppf_sinh_cosh

Compute hyperbolic sine and cosine into two outputs.

    ppf_t *sop,
    ppf_t *cop,
    const ppf_t *op,
    ppf_rnd_t rnd,

);

Result. Test for PPF_TERNARY_ERROR before decoding. Allocation and failure. An unrecovered project-allocation failure preserves the prior numerical output. Sticky flags may change, and an exact fallback may succeed while retaining the allocation flag. Numerical rejection is a separate case and may commit NaN.

Resource policy. special-function certification uses bounded precision escalation; several series and recurrences are capped at 1,000,000 iterations; dyadic interval construction permits at most 1,000,000 extra endpoint-alignment bits and retries or rejects unusable certificates. Consult the numerical-limits appendix for the complete cap inventory.

17.21.16 ppf_get_constant_interval

Export a certified dyadic interval around a supported constant.

int ppf_get_constant_interval(
    ppf_constant_id_t id,
    mpz_ptr lower,
    mpz_ptr upper,
    ppf_exp_t *exponent,
    ppf_prec_t precision,
    unsigned long workers
);

Result. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. The certified dyadic interval is written to lower, upper, and exponent. Failure indicator: -1.

Overlap. lower and upper may refer to distinct caller-owned integers; Forbidden: lower and upper must not be the same mpz object.

Allocation and failure. Unrecovered project-allocation failure before publication preserves lower, upper, and exponent and releases temporary project-owned storage; GMP allocation while copying successful outputs is outside this recoverable allocation contract.

Resource policy. constant certification uses at most 16 precision-escalation attempts per request. Consult the numerical-limits appendix for the complete cap inventory.

Concurrency. The library synchronizes its global state. Caller-owned mutable objects still require exclusive access.

17.22 Certified interval assignment

17.22.1 ppf_set_dyadic_interval

Round a certified dyadic interval into a destination, reporting decided, undecided, or error.

ppf_interval_status_t ppf_set_dyadic_interval(
    ppf_t *rop,
    mpz_srcptr lower,
    mpz_srcptr upper,
    ppf_exp_t exponent,
    ppf_rnd_t rnd,
    int *ternary,
    ppf_context_t *ctx
);

Input contract. lower and upper are exact integers with lower <= upper and share the supplied binary exponent.

Result. PPF_INTERVAL_DECIDED, PPF_INTERVAL_UNDECIDED, or PPF_INTERVAL_ERROR. The numerical ternary is a separate output.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context. PPF_RND_DEFAULT resolves through the supplied context or the calling thread default context.

Allocation and failure. An unrecovered project-allocation failure preserves the prior numerical output. Sticky flags may change, and an exact fallback may succeed while retaining the allocation flag. Numerical rejection is a separate case and may commit NaN.

17.23 Core comparison, validation, and diagnostics

17.23.1 ppf_cmp

Compare two Polyphase values.

int ppf_cmp(const ppf_t *a, const ppf_t *b, ppf_context_t *ctx);

Result. An ordering result. NaNs and unordered comparisons require the operation’s documented handling.

Context and rounding. A null ctx selects the calling thread’s default context.

17.23.2 ppf_dump

Write an internal diagnostic representation to standard output.

void ppf_dump(const ppf_t *x);

Result. No return value.

17.23.3 ppf_dump_file

Write an internal diagnostic representation to a selected stream.

void ppf_dump_file(FILE *stream, const ppf_t *x);

Result. No return value.

17.23.4 ppf_equal_p

Test exact equality of represented values.

int ppf_equal_p(const ppf_t *a, const ppf_t *b);

Result. A predicate result: zero means false and a nonzero value means true.

17.23.5 ppf_kind_name

Return a readable name for a value kind.

const char *ppf_kind_name(ppf_kind_t kind);

Result. A borrowed pointer. Do not free the returned storage. Failure indicator: NULL where documented.

Ownership. returned string is library-owned static storage.

17.23.6 ppf_rounding_name

Return a readable name for a rounding mode.

const char *ppf_rounding_name(ppf_rnd_t rnd);

Result. Returns a static name for the supplied enumeration value, including PPF_RND_DEFAULT. An invalid enumeration value returns the static string PPF_RND_INVALID; this function does not return NULL.

Context and rounding. the enumeration is inspected without selecting or resolving a rounding policy; PPF_RND_DEFAULT has its own literal name.

Ownership. returned string is library-owned static storage.

17.23.7 ppf_validate

Check internal representation invariants.

int ppf_validate(const ppf_t *x);

Result. A predicate result: zero means false and a nonzero value means true.

19 Types and named constants

Include the installed public header to obtain these declarations. The listings below are reference material. The installed header is the authoritative declaration source. These definitions summarize the governed public types. Public layout compatibility does not make direct field mutation an ordinary application interface. Use lifecycle and setter functions unless you are implementing the documented direct-storage protocol.

19.1 Scalar types

#if PPF_HAVE_DECIMAL_FLOAT
__extension__ typedef _Decimal128 ppf_decimal128_t;
#endif
#if PPF_HAVE_DECIMAL_FLOAT
__extension__ typedef _Decimal64 ppf_decimal64_t;
#endif
typedef int64_t ppf_exp_t;
typedef uint32_t ppf_flags_t;
#if PPF_HAVE_FLOAT128
__extension__ typedef __float128 ppf_float128_t;
#endif
typedef uint64_t ppf_prec_t;

The optional decimal and 128-bit binary types exist only when their installed-header capability conditions are satisfied. They do not make those C extensions mandatory for the independent core.

19.3 Precision, range, and ABI constants

Version and digest strings identify a build or generated contract. They are not mathematical parameters and do not attest to the bytes of a loaded binary.

#define PPF_ABI_EPOCH 1
#define PPF_ABI_INFO_VERSION 1
#define PPF_ABI_REVISION 0
#define PPF_ABI_TAG "polyphase-float-abi-1"
#define PPF_ALIASING_CONTRACT_VERSION 1
#define PPF_EMAX_DEFAULT ((ppf_exp_t) 1073741823)
#define PPF_EMAX_MAX ((ppf_exp_t)(INT64_MAX / 4))
#define PPF_EMIN_DEFAULT ((ppf_exp_t)-1073741823)
#define PPF_EMIN_MIN ((ppf_exp_t)(INT64_MIN / 4))
#define PPF_PREC_DEFAULT ((ppf_prec_t)53)
#define PPF_SEMANTIC_CONTRACT_VERSION 1
#define PPF_TERNARY_ERROR INT_MIN

19.4 Public layout records

The allocator function-pointer types and advanced custom-storage callbacks are declared in <polyphase_float.h>. Keep callback signatures exact. The records below describe ABI shape, not a license to replace initialized objects with raw structure copies.

20 Complete example programs

These are the complete source files supplied with the manual. Build them through the manual example targets or the checked-example runner. They include their own initialization, status checks, output, and cleanup. Each program’s expected output is recorded in the example manifest and the example-results guide.

20.1 intro_first.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t a = {0}, b = {0}, product = {0};
    int status = 1;
    int ternary;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) {
        fputs("Cannot initialize the context.\n", stderr);
        return 1;
    }
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&a, 128, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&b, 128, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&product, 128, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_set_ui(&a, 2, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR ||
        ppf_set_ui(&b, 3, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;

    ternary = ppf_mul(&product, &a, &b, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    if (ternary != 0 || ppf_cmp_ui(&product, 6, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (fputs("2 * 3 = ", stdout) == EOF ||
        ppf_out_str(stdout, 10, 6, &product, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0 ||
        fputc('\n', stdout) == EOF || fflush(stdout) == EOF)
        goto cleanup;
    status = 0;

cleanup:
    if (status != 0) fputs("The calculation or output failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&product);
    ppf_clear(&b);
    ppf_clear(&a);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.2 intro_flags.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t one = {0}, three = {0}, zero = {0}, result = {0};
    ppf_flags_t flags;
    int status = 1;
    int ternary;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&one, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&three, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&zero, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&result, 8, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_set_ui(&one, 1, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR ||
        ppf_set_ui(&three, 3, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;
    ppf_set_zero(&zero, 1);
    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);

    ternary = ppf_div(&result, &one, &three, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    flags = ppf_context_flags(&ctx);
    if (ternary == 0 || (flags & PPF_FLAG_INEXACT) == 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (puts("1 / 3: INEXACT is set") == EOF) goto cleanup;

    ternary = ppf_set_ui(&result, 2, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    if (ternary != 0 ||
        (ppf_context_flags(&ctx) & PPF_FLAG_INEXACT) == 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (puts("exact assignment: INEXACT is still set") == EOF)
        goto cleanup;

    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    if (ppf_context_flags(&ctx) != 0) goto cleanup;
    if (puts("after clearing: no flags are set") == EOF) goto cleanup;

    ternary = ppf_div(&result, &one, &zero, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    flags = ppf_context_flags(&ctx);
    if (!ppf_inf_p(&result) || ppf_signbit(&result) ||
        (flags & PPF_FLAG_DIVBY0) == 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (puts("1 / 0: positive infinity; DIVBY0 is set") == EOF)
        goto cleanup;

    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    ternary = ppf_div(&result, &zero, &zero, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    flags = ppf_context_flags(&ctx);
    if (!ppf_nan_p(&result) || (flags & PPF_FLAG_NAN) == 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (puts("0 / 0: NaN; NAN is set") == EOF || fflush(stdout) == EOF)
        goto cleanup;
    status = 0;

cleanup:
    if (status != 0) fputs("The flag example failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&result);
    ppf_clear(&zero);
    ppf_clear(&three);
    ppf_clear(&one);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.3 intro_precision.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>

static int print_value(const char *label, const ppf_t *value,
                       ppf_context_t *ctx) {
    if (fputs(label, stdout) == EOF ||
        ppf_out_str(stdout, 10, 12, value, PPF_RNDN, ctx) == 0 ||
        fputc('\n', stdout) == EOF)
        return -1;
    return 0;
}

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t coarse = {0}, widened = {0}, fresh = {0};
    int status = 1;
    int ternary;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&coarse, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&widened, 128, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&fresh, 128, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    /* set_str returns a status, unlike the ternary-returning set. */
    if (ppf_set_str(&coarse, "0.1", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_set_str(&fresh, "0.1", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    ternary = ppf_set(&widened, &coarse, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) goto cleanup;
    if (ternary != 0 || ppf_cmp(&coarse, &widened, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_cmp(&widened, &fresh, &ctx) == 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_context_set_default_precision(&ctx, 256) != 0 ||
        ppf_get_prec(&coarse) != 8 || ppf_get_prec(&fresh) != 128)
        goto cleanup;
    if (print_value("parsed at 8 bits     = ", &coarse, &ctx) != 0 ||
        print_value("copied to 128 bits   = ", &widened, &ctx) != 0 ||
        print_value("parsed at 128 bits   = ", &fresh, &ctx) != 0 ||
        puts("changing the default leaves existing precisions unchanged") == EOF ||
        fflush(stdout) == EOF)
        goto cleanup;
    status = 0;

cleanup:
    if (status != 0) fputs("The precision example failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&fresh);
    ppf_clear(&widened);
    ppf_clear(&coarse);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.4 intro_rounding.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>

static int print_result(const char *label, const ppf_t *value,
                        int ternary, ppf_context_t *ctx) {
    const char *direction;
    if (ternary == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR) return -1;
    direction = ternary < 0 ? "below" : ternary > 0 ? "above" : "exact";
    if (fputs(label, stdout) == EOF ||
        ppf_out_str(stdout, 10, 9, value, PPF_RNDN, ctx) == 0 ||
        fprintf(stdout, " (%s)\n", direction) < 0)
        return -1;
    return 0;
}

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t one = {0}, three = {0};
    ppf_t lower = {0}, nearest = {0}, upper = {0};
    int down, near, up;
    int status = 1;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&one, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&three, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&lower, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&nearest, 8, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&upper, 8, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_set_ui(&one, 1, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR ||
        ppf_set_ui(&three, 3, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;
    down = ppf_div(&lower, &one, &three, PPF_RNDD, &ctx);
    near = ppf_div(&nearest, &one, &three, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    up = ppf_div(&upper, &one, &three, PPF_RNDU, &ctx);
    if (down == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR || near == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR ||
        up == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;
    if (!(down < 0 && near > 0 && up > 0) ||
        ppf_cmp(&lower, &upper, &ctx) >= 0 ||
        ppf_cmp(&nearest, &upper, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (print_result("down    = ", &lower, down, &ctx) != 0 ||
        print_result("nearest = ", &nearest, near, &ctx) != 0 ||
        print_result("up      = ", &upper, up, &ctx) != 0 ||
        fflush(stdout) == EOF)
        goto cleanup;
    status = 0;

cleanup:
    if (status != 0) fputs("The rounding example failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&upper);
    ppf_clear(&nearest);
    ppf_clear(&lower);
    ppf_clear(&three);
    ppf_clear(&one);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.5 numeric_constants.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#define REQUIRE(c) do { if (!(c)) goto cleanup; } while (0)
int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t direct = {0}, certified = {0};
    mpz_t lower, upper;
    ppf_exp_t exponent = 0;
    int status = 1, direct_t, interval_t = 0;
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    mpz_inits(lower, upper, NULL);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&direct, 80, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&certified, 80, &ctx) == 0);
    direct_t = ppf_const_pi(&direct, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(direct_t != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR);
    /* Interval export is a status API using the thread-default context. */
    REQUIRE(ppf_get_constant_interval(PPF_CONSTANT_PI, lower, upper,
                                      &exponent, 160, 1) == 0);
    REQUIRE(mpz_cmp(lower, upper) <= 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_dyadic_interval(&certified, lower, upper, exponent,
                PPF_RNDN, &interval_t, &ctx) == PPF_INTERVAL_DECIDED);
    REQUIRE(ppf_equal_p(&direct, &certified));
    REQUIRE((direct_t > 0) == (interval_t > 0));
    REQUIRE((direct_t < 0) == (interval_t < 0));
    puts("Pi: direct evaluation and exported interval agree at 80 bits.");
    puts("The interval proves the value and its rounding direction.");
    status = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status) fputs("Constant example failed.\n", stderr);
    mpz_clears(lower, upper, NULL);
    ppf_clear(&direct); ppf_clear(&certified);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx); ppf_free_constant_caches(); ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.6 numeric_elementary.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#define REQUIRE(c) do { if (!(c)) goto cleanup; } while (0)
#define NUMBER_CALL(c) REQUIRE((c) != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t x = {0}, one = {0}, sum = {0}, result = {0}, pi = {0};
    int status = 1;
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&x, 53, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&one, 53, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&sum, 53, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&result, 53, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&pi, 53, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui_2exp(&x, 1, -80, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui(&one, 1, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    NUMBER_CALL(ppf_add(&sum, &one, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx));
    REQUIRE(ppf_equal_p(&sum, &one));
    NUMBER_CALL(ppf_log(&result, &sum, PPF_RNDN, &ctx));
    REQUIRE(ppf_zero_p(&result));
    puts("log of the rounded 1 + 2^-80 is zero at 53 bits.");
    NUMBER_CALL(ppf_log1p(&result, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx));
    REQUIRE(ppf_regular_p(&result) && !ppf_signbit(&result));
    NUMBER_CALL(ppf_expm1(&result, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx));
    REQUIRE(ppf_regular_p(&result) && !ppf_signbit(&result));
    puts("log1p(2^-80) and expm1(2^-80) remain positive.");
    REQUIRE(ppf_sinpi(&result, &one, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_zero_p(&result));
    NUMBER_CALL(ppf_const_pi(&pi, PPF_RNDN, &ctx));
    NUMBER_CALL(ppf_sin(&result, &pi, PPF_RNDN, &ctx));
    REQUIRE(ppf_regular_p(&result));
    puts("sinpi(1) is exactly zero; sin of rounded pi is not.");
    status = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status) fputs("Elementary-function example failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&x); ppf_clear(&one); ppf_clear(&sum);
    ppf_clear(&result); ppf_clear(&pi);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx); ppf_free_constant_caches(); ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.7 numeric_import.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <float.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#define REQUIRE(c) do { if (!(c)) goto cleanup; } while (0)
int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t decimal = {0}, native = {0};
    mpq_t target, qdecimal, qnative, edecimal, enative, widened;
    int status = 1;
    if (FLT_RADIX != 2 || DBL_MANT_DIG != 53) {
        fputs("This example requires a 53-bit binary double.\n", stderr);
        return 1;
    }
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    mpq_inits(target, qdecimal, qnative, edecimal, enative, widened, NULL);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&decimal, 256, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&native, 256, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_str(&decimal, "0.1", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_d(&native, 0.1, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    mpq_set_ui(target, 1, 10);
    ppf_get_q(qdecimal, &decimal, &ctx);
    ppf_get_q(qnative, &native, &ctx);
    mpq_sub(edecimal, qdecimal, target); mpq_abs(edecimal, edecimal);
    mpq_sub(enative, qnative, target); mpq_abs(enative, enative);
    REQUIRE(mpq_sgn(edecimal) != 0 && mpq_sgn(enative) != 0);
    REQUIRE(mpq_cmp(edecimal, enative) < 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_prec_round(&native, 512, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    ppf_get_q(widened, &native, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(mpq_equal(qnative, widened));
    puts("Neither binary value is exactly 1/10.");
    puts("The 256-bit decimal parse is closer to 1/10.");
    puts("Widening the native import preserves its old value.");
    status = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status) fputs("Import example failed.\n", stderr);
    mpq_clears(target, qdecimal, qnative, edecimal, enative, widened, NULL);
    ppf_clear(&decimal); ppf_clear(&native);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx); ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.8 numeric_ranges.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#define REQUIRE(c) do { if (!(c)) goto cleanup; } while (0)
int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t a = {0}, b = {0}, result = {0};
    int status = 1, t;
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&a, 8, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&b, 8, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&result, 2, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_context_set_range(&ctx, -9, 9) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui(&a, 7, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui_2exp(&b, 15, -10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    t = ppf_div(&result, &a, &b, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(t != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR && t > 0 && ppf_inf_p(&result));
    REQUIRE(ppf_context_flags(&ctx) == (PPF_FLAG_OVERFLOW | PPF_FLAG_INEXACT));
    puts("Nearest quotient: +infinity; overflow and inexact.");
    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    t = ppf_div(&result, &a, &b, PPF_RNDZ, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(t != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR && t < 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_cmp_ui(&result, 384, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_context_flags(&ctx) == PPF_FLAG_INEXACT);
    puts("Toward-zero quotient: 384; inexact only.");
    REQUIRE(ppf_context_set_range(&ctx, -30, 100) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui_2exp(&result, 1, -31, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    t = ppf_subnormalize(&result, 0, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(t == 0 && ppf_context_flags(&ctx) == PPF_FLAG_UNDERFLOW);
    puts("Exact subnormal emulation: underflow without inexact.");
    status = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status) fputs("Range example failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&a); ppf_clear(&b); ppf_clear(&result);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx); ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.9 numeric_refinement.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#define REQUIRE(c) do { if (!(c)) goto cleanup; } while (0)
int main(void) {
    const unsigned scales[] = {8, 16, 32, 64, 128};
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t result = {0};
    mpz_t radicand, lower, upper, remainder;
    int status = 1, ternary = 777, decided = 0;
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    mpz_inits(radicand, lower, upper, remainder, NULL);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&result, 53, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui(&result, 1, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(scales) / sizeof(scales[0]); ++i) {
        unsigned k = scales[i];
        mpz_set_ui(radicand, 2);
        mpz_mul_2exp(radicand, radicand, 2u * k);
        mpz_sqrtrem(lower, remainder, radicand);
        REQUIRE(mpz_sgn(remainder) > 0);
        mpz_add_ui(upper, lower, 1);
        ppf_interval_status_t s = ppf_set_dyadic_interval(
            &result, lower, upper, -(ppf_exp_t)k, PPF_RNDN, &ternary, &ctx);
        REQUIRE(s != PPF_INTERVAL_ERROR);
        if (s == PPF_INTERVAL_UNDECIDED) {
            REQUIRE(ternary == 777 && ppf_cmp_ui(&result, 1, &ctx) == 0);
            printf("scale %u: refine\n", k);
        } else {
            REQUIRE(ternary > 0);
            printf("scale %u: certified 53-bit sqrt(2), rounded upward\n", k);
            decided = 1;
            break;
        }
    }
    REQUIRE(decided);
    status = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status) fputs("Refinement example did not obtain its certificate.\n", stderr);
    mpz_clears(radicand, lower, upper, remainder, NULL);
    ppf_clear(&result); ppf_context_clear(&ctx); ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.10 numeric_special_domains.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
#include "polyphase_float.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#define REQUIRE(c) do { if (!(c)) goto cleanup; } while (0)
int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t x = {0}, result = {0};
    int status = 1, t, gamma_sign = 0;
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return 1;
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&x, 80, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_init2_ctx(&result, 80, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui(&x, 5, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_gamma(&result, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_cmp_ui(&result, 24, &ctx) == 0);
    puts("Gamma(5) = 24 exactly.");
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_si_2exp(&x, -1, -1, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    t = ppf_lgamma(&result, &gamma_sign, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(t != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR && ppf_regular_p(&result));
    REQUIRE(gamma_sign == -1);
    puts("lgamma(-1/2) returns a finite log magnitude and sign -1.");
    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    t = ppf_lngamma(&result, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(t != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR && ppf_nan_p(&result));
    REQUIRE((ppf_context_flags(&ctx) & PPF_FLAG_NAN) != 0);
    puts("lngamma(-1/2) reports a real-domain NaN.");
    REQUIRE(ppf_set_ui(&x, 501, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0);
    REQUIRE(ppf_cmpabs_ui(&x, 500, &ctx) > 0);
    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    t = ppf_ai(&result, &x, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    REQUIRE(t == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR);
    REQUIRE((ppf_context_flags(&ctx) & PPF_FLAG_ERANGE) != 0);
    REQUIRE((ppf_context_flags(&ctx) & PPF_FLAG_ALLOC) == 0);
    puts("Ai(501) exceeds the implementation domain: ERANGE, not ALLOC.");
    status = 0;
cleanup:
    if (status) fputs("Special-function example failed.\n", stderr);
    ppf_clear(&x); ppf_clear(&result); ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_free_constant_caches(); ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return status;
}

20.11 systems_allocation.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
/* Core-only example: one controlled allocation failure and recovery. */
#include <polyphase_float.h>

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct {
    int fail_next;
    size_t live_blocks;
} allocation_state;

static void *tracked_malloc(void *opaque, size_t bytes) {
    allocation_state *state = opaque;
    void *block;
    if (state->fail_next) { state->fail_next = 0; return NULL; }
    block = malloc(bytes);
    if (block) ++state->live_blocks;
    return block;
}

static void *tracked_realloc(void *opaque, void *block,
                             size_t old_bytes, size_t new_bytes) {
    allocation_state *state = opaque;
    int was_null = block == NULL;
    void *replacement;
    (void)old_bytes;
    if (state->fail_next) { state->fail_next = 0; return NULL; }
    replacement = realloc(block, new_bytes);
    if (replacement && was_null) ++state->live_blocks;
    return replacement;
}

static void tracked_free(void *opaque, void *block, size_t bytes) {
    allocation_state *state = opaque;
    (void)bytes;
    if (block) { --state->live_blocks; free(block); }
}

int main(void) {
    allocation_state state = {0, 0};
    ppf_allocator_t allocator = {
        tracked_malloc, tracked_realloc, tracked_free, &state
    };
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t value = {0};
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    if (ppf_context_init_custom(&ctx, &allocator) != 0) return status;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&value, 80, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_set_ui(&value, 37, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;

    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    state.fail_next = 1;
    if (ppf_set_str(&value, "1.25", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == 0 ||
        state.fail_next != 0 || ppf_cmp_ui(&value, 37, &ctx) != 0 ||
        !(ppf_context_flags(&ctx) & PPF_FLAG_ALLOC)) goto cleanup;

    ppf_context_flags_clear(&ctx, PPF_FLAGS_ALL);
    if (ppf_set_str(&value, "1.25", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_cmp_d(&value, 1.25, &ctx) != 0 ||
        (ppf_context_flags(&ctx) & PPF_FLAG_ALLOC)) goto cleanup;
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    ppf_clear(&value);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    if (state.live_blocks != 0) status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    if (status == EXIT_SUCCESS) {
        if (puts("allocation failure preserved 37; retry produced 1.25") == EOF)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    } else {
        fputs("allocation example failed\n", stderr);
    }
    return status;
}

20.12 systems_io.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
/* Core-only example: text ownership and a PPFIF round trip. */
#include <polyphase_float.h>

#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t value = {0}, restored = {0};
    ppf_exp_t exponent = 0;
    char *digits = NULL, *formatted = NULL;
    FILE *record = NULL;
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return status;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&value, 80, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_init2_ctx(&restored, 17, &ctx) != 0) goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_set_str(&value, "1.25", 10, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0)
        goto cleanup;

    digits = ppf_get_str(NULL, &exponent, 10, 5, &value, PPF_RNDN, &ctx);
    if (!digits || strcmp(digits, "12500") != 0 || exponent != 1)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_asprintf(&formatted, "value=%.2RNf", &value) < 0 ||
        !formatted || strcmp(formatted, "value=1.25") != 0) goto cleanup;

    record = tmpfile();
    if (!record || ppf_fpif_export(record, &value) != 0 ||
        fflush(record) != 0 || fseek(record, 0L, SEEK_SET) != 0)
        goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_fpif_import(&restored, record, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_cmp(&restored, &value, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_get_prec(&restored) != ppf_get_prec(&value)) goto cleanup;
    if (fclose(record) != 0) { record = NULL; goto cleanup; }
    record = NULL;

    if (printf("digits=%s exponent=%" PRId64 "\n", digits, exponent) < 0 ||
        puts(formatted) == EOF ||
        puts("PPFIF round trip: value and precision preserved") == EOF)
        goto cleanup;
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    if (record) (void)fclose(record);
    free(formatted);
    ppf_free_str(digits);
    ppf_clear(&restored);
    ppf_clear(&value);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    if (status != EXIT_SUCCESS) fputs("I/O example failed\n", stderr);
    return status;
}

20.13 systems_mpfr_bridge.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
/* Requires the MPFR adapter, official MPFR headers, and the core library. */
#include <polyphase_float_mpfr.h>

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t value = {0};
    mpfr_t input, output;
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return status;
    mpfr_init2(input, 128);
    mpfr_init2(output, 53);
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&value, 53, &ctx) != 0) goto cleanup;
    if (mpfr_set_ui(input, 5, MPFR_RNDN) != 0 ||
        mpfr_div_ui(input, input, 4, MPFR_RNDN) != 0) goto cleanup;
    if (ppf_import_mpfr_exact(&value, input, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_get_prec(&value) != 128 ||
        ppf_mul_ui(&value, &value, 8, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_get_mpfr(output, &value, MPFR_RNDN) != 0 ||
        mpfr_cmp_ui(output, 10) != 0) goto cleanup;
    status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    ppf_clear(&value);
    mpfr_clear(output);
    mpfr_clear(input);
    mpfr_free_cache();
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    if (status == EXIT_SUCCESS) {
        if (puts("MPFR -> Polyphase -> MPFR: 10") == EOF)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    } else {
        fputs("MPFR bridge example failed\n", stderr);
    }
    return status;
}

20.14 systems_threads.c

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-3.0-or-later */
/* Core + POSIX threads: shared immutable input, private mutable state. */
#include <polyphase_float.h>

#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct {
    const ppf_t *input;
    int success;
} worker_arguments;

static void *square_worker(void *opaque) {
    worker_arguments *args = opaque;
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t result = {0};
    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return NULL;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&result, 80, &ctx) == 0 &&
        ppf_sqr(&result, args->input, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) != PPF_TERNARY_ERROR &&
        ppf_cmp_ui(&result, 49, &ctx) == 0)
        args->success = 1;
    ppf_clear(&result);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    return NULL;
}

int main(void) {
    ppf_context_t ctx;
    ppf_t input = {0};
    pthread_t threads[2];
    worker_arguments args[2] = {{&input, 0}, {&input, 0}};
    unsigned started = 0;
    int status = EXIT_FAILURE;

    if (ppf_context_init(&ctx) != 0) return status;
    if (ppf_init2_ctx(&input, 80, &ctx) != 0 ||
        ppf_set_ui(&input, 7, PPF_RNDN, &ctx) == PPF_TERNARY_ERROR)
        goto cleanup;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
        if (pthread_create(&threads[i], NULL, square_worker, &args[i]) != 0)
            break;
        ++started;
    }
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < started; ++i) {
        /* Do not release a shared input unless every reader has joined. */
        if (pthread_join(threads[i], NULL) != 0) {
            fputs("could not join a worker\n", stderr);
            return EXIT_FAILURE;
        }
    }
    if (started == 2 && args[0].success && args[1].success)
        status = EXIT_SUCCESS;

cleanup:
    ppf_clear(&input);
    ppf_context_clear(&ctx);
    ppf_thread_cleanup();
    if (status == EXIT_SUCCESS) {
        if (puts("2 workers read one immutable input; both produced 49") == EOF)
            status = EXIT_FAILURE;
    } else {
        fputs("thread example failed\n", stderr);
    }
    return status;
}

21 Glossary

ABI. The application binary interface: calling conventions, symbol names, public object layouts, enum values, and related requirements that let an already compiled application use a compatible library.

Aliasing. Two arguments refer to the same object or to overlapping storage. An allowed single-output in-place operation does not imply that two distinct outputs may be collapsed into one object.

Allocator provenance. The identity and state of the allocator that owns an allocation. Return storage through its documented release function rather than choosing a deallocator by the pointer’s C type.

Arbitrary precision. The application chooses the finite significand precision. This is not infinite precision, unlimited memory, or a guarantee that every difficult operation will certify at every requested precision.

Binary exponent. The power of two that scales a binary significand. The library’s normalized exponent conventions and configured bounds determine range behavior. A decimal output exponent uses its own stated radix.

Borrowed storage. Memory the caller may access subject to lifetime rules but does not own and must not release. Changing the owning object can invalidate an object-storage pointer.

Certificate. An enclosure or other exact mathematical evidence used to justify a rounded result. Certification can remain undecided within the available precision or resource budget.

Context. The configuration and state used by operations: defaults, rounding, exponent bounds, sticky flags, allocator callbacks, and working storage. An explicit mutable context requires exclusive access.

Correct rounding. The stored result equals the result of rounding the exact mathematical value once to the selected representable set and rule. This property is stronger than observing agreement at two working precisions.

Destination precision. The precision attached to the output object. Passing a higher-precision context does not silently enlarge an existing destination. Some named precision-changing operations have explicit rules.

Directed rounding. Rounding toward positive infinity, negative infinity, zero, or away from zero. For a negative value, toward positive infinity and away from zero point in different directions.

Dyadic. An integer or rational scaled by an integer power of two. Every finite binary floating-point value is a dyadic rational.

Exact input. The mathematical value represented by the supplied data. Importing a C double exactly preserves that binary double, including its earlier rounding. It does not recover an intended decimal value.

Exponent range. The configured interval used by operations to classify and settle their output. Range limits, storage limits, and precision limits are separate constraints.

Faithful rounding. Selection of an allowed neighboring representable value. It is not the same contract as the unique nearest or directed result, and its ternary output must be interpreted under the faithful-mode rules.

Flag. A sticky diagnostic bit in context state. Flags can outlive the operation that raised them. Clear or save them deliberately when attributing a diagnostic to one computation.

Fused operation. An operation that combines its terms before a final rounding, rather than rounding each intermediate expression separately. Its result can differ from a sequence of individually rounded calls.

GMP. The GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library. Polyphase uses its integer and rational machinery. GMP’s own allocation behavior is outside the recoverable project-allocator rollback contract.

Guard precision. Extra working precision used inside an algorithm. It does not by itself prove that a final result is correctly rounded.

Inexact. The stored numerical result differs from the exact value in the operation’s contract. Conversion and formatting can introduce their own rounding steps.

Interval settlement. Deciding whether every exact value in a supplied enclosure has a common rounded output, compatible ternary direction, and the required common range-flag state. An undecided result asks for better evidence, not a guessed midpoint.

LP64. The supported C data model in which long and pointers are 64 bits while int is 32 bits. This differs from native 64-bit Windows’ usual LLP64 model.

MPFR. A separate multiple-precision floating-point library. Polyphase’s optional adapter imports and exports its values; the independent production core does not need it. Differential test agreement is finite execution evidence, not a replacement for mathematical arguments.

NaN. Not a Number, a special value used for invalid numerical results and some numerical-rejection paths. Inspect status and flags to understand the particular outcome.

Nearest, ties to even. Select the nearest representable value. At an exact midpoint choose the candidate whose retained least-significant significand bit is even.

Numerical rejection. An operation cannot produce a certified result under its resource or admission policy. It may return PPF_TERNARY_ERROR, raise PPF_FLAG_ERANGE, and commit NaN. This differs from allocation rollback.

Precision. The number of bits available in the significand, including the leading significant bit. The rough decimal information capacity is precision * log10(2), not a promise that a chosen decimal expression has that many correct digits.

PPFIF. Polyphase’s binary interchange format. Its import contract includes admission limits and validation before committing the numerical destination.

Remainder bound. A bound on terms omitted from a finite series or asymptotic expression. A decreasing term or a small last term is not alone a universal remainder proof.

Representable neighbor. The adjacent value in the destination’s precision and range model. Spacing changes with binary exponent.

SONAME. The ELF shared-library name recorded for runtime loading. The project’s release version and its governed ABI SONAME need not have the same major number.

Status return. A success or failure code, predicate, count, or other non-ternary return. An int declaration alone does not identify a numerical ternary. In particular, ppf_set_str and ppf_strtofr have different return contracts.

Sticky diagnostic. A diagnostic that remains set until explicitly cleared or restored. A successful later operation does not erase it.

Subnormalization. The explicit operation that implements the library’s reduced-precision range semantics when requested. An exact reduced-precision result can still raise underflow under that operation’s contract, while inexactness depends on the rounding relation.

Ternary. A numerical return whose sign compares the stored result with the exact result. Zero means exact, negative means below, and positive means above, subject to the selected rounding contract. The error sentinel is not a numerical direction.

Thread default. State owned by the calling thread and selected by APIs that permit a null context. It is distinct from an application-owned explicit context and from global synchronized caches.

Transactional allocation failure. An unrecovered project-allocation failure preserves the prior numerical destination under the operation’s documented contract. This does not undo file I/O, kernel effects, GMP failure, or arbitrary application callbacks.

ULP. A unit in the last retained place, measured at a specified precision and exponent. It is not a fixed absolute distance over the whole number line.

Working precision. The precision used to construct intermediate evidence or values. It may exceed the destination precision and may increase during bounded certification attempts.
